Sports.title: ‘Absolutely pathetic’ – Fuming Gary Neville slams Man Utd after ‘worst 15 minutes I’ve ever seen them play’
Sports.content:
GRUMPY GARY ‘Absolutely pathetic’ – Fuming Gary Neville slams Man Utd after ‘worst 15 minutes I’ve ever seen them play’







Next

GARY NEVILLE tore into “absolutely pathetic” Manchester United for the worst 15 minutes he has ever seen from the club.

Then he doubled down after full-time by blasting the flops as a “disgrace”.



The legendary right-back was on commentary duties for his former side’s trip to West London to face Fulham.

After a goalless first half, United fell behind on 63 minutes when Senne Lammens bundled the ball and Lisandro Martinez scored a woeful own goal.



It came as Fulham launched an attack when Calvin Bassey outmuscled Matheus Cunha to win possession.

That capped off a dreadful beginning to the second half, with Neville slamming Michael Carrick’s Red Devils for being “mannequins” and walking around in defence showing zero urgency, passion or quality.

And the Sky Sports pundit did not hold back in the aftermath of the goal – insisting it was the most terrible spell in 46 years.

The 51-year-old fumed: “I’ve watched Manchester United since the age of five and that’s the worst 15 minutes I have ever seen them play.

“Absolutely pathetic. They have walked for 15 minutes and you get what you deserve in a football match.

“Maybe there will be a reaction but I’ve never seen a lack of effort for 15 to 20 minutes like I have just seen there.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

“What must he (Carrick) be thinking?

“He probably cannot believe what he has watched in those last 15 or 20 minutes. He’s got to act now.”

Minutes earlier, he had said: “It’s a few minutes of the blue mannequins playing against the white mannequins and then it switches around, bizarre football match.

“They won’t go anywhere with a lack of urgency like this. I don’t know if it’s fear or complacency, they’re just not working hard.”

Ashley Young insisted United need to show intensity and intent from the first minute, not the 63rd – and Fulham running 6km further than United was “unacceptable”.



Louis Saha then described the United performance as like that during a “charity match”.

United ended up taking 29 shots with just six on target at Craven Cottage.

And one of the last, a speculative strike from Cunha in the 89th minute, took a wicked deflection to avoid defeat and rescue a point.

But that was enough to disguise the reality of the lack of effort in Neville’s eyes.



Joining the others in the Sky studio, he reiterated his anger.

Neville continued: “I’ve never seen a Manchester United team walk out of possession as much as that.

“Michael just said there that he was happy with the team’s energy. Michael’s got to stop defending them.

“I called them mannequins. They were absolutely mannequins. I’ve never seen a Manchester United team for 15 minutes walk around out of possession as much as that. No alertness, no liveliness.

“He’s got too many players in the team, and I actually wish he could play those attacking players, but they’re going to kill him defensively.



“Very rarely do I say that a team doesn’t work hard or is lacking in effort, because that’s the ultimate criticism that you can give a group of players.

“But that first 15 minutes of that second half, Manchester United without the ball, and generally for the first 60 minutes, were an absolute disgrace. Nowhere near good enough.”

He then went on to add: “You talk about Manchester United having 26 shots, Fulham could have scored four or five goals as well.



“Manchester United were walking out on that pitch, all of them in that first 15 minutes of that second half. That is not acceptable.

“I hope Michael is giving them a real grilling behind the scenes in respect of that performance because that type of work ethic and lack of running will land Michael in a lot of trouble.

“The reason I refer to the word ‘disgrace’ is because when I see teams not running for 15 minutes, I think of that as being a disgrace. Not running is the only thing that I will call a disgrace.

“Both teams were the worst I’ve seen defensively in the Premier League this season by a long way.

“They’ve got to work harder than that for him. I am absolutely not changing my mind on that.



“I played for the club for 25 years under a guise of, ‘We want world-class players who work like League Two players.’ That’s it.”

Then Carrick hit back at suggestions his team were too passive.

The boss said: “I didn’t think we were. Did you think we were?

“Football is a difficult game. We controlled a lot of the first half.

“It’s the Premier League and you will have spells where you don’t have it all your own way.



“To expect total dominance for the whole game, I don’t think anyone gets that in this league.

“I thought we should have won the game, I thought we created enough to win the game.

“We came to get the win of course, the way it panned out and the way we finished is the positive we take from it.”

Sports.title: Man Utd player ratings: Lisandro Martinez and Marcus Rashford suffer horror show with Cunha best of a bad bunch
Sports.content:
Next

MANCHESTER UNITED salvaged a late 1-1 draw as Fulham narrowly missed out on their first Premier League win of the season.

In a week where Michael Carrick‘s side lost a 50 year record at Old Trafford, Matheus Cunha’s deflected strike in the 89th minute saved United from a first defeat at Craven Cottage since 2009.



Lisandro Martinez’s embarrassing own goal after Senne Lammens parried out Calvin Bassey‘s shot in the 63rd minute summed up a dreadful afternoon for the Red Devils.

Here’s how SunSport’s Katherine Walsh rated the out-worked United players at a sunny Craven Cottage.



Senne Lammens – 6

The Belgian was United’s best player before a pathetic mistake saw him push out the ball to Martinez for Fulham‘s opener. Before that, Lammens came up with several saves with his hand and foot.

Was kept busy by his backline’s vulnerabilities and Fulham didn’t have their shooting boots on. Denied Kevin after United went behind but Bernd Leno perhaps a better afternoon.



Diogo Dalot – 4

Alex Iwobi won’t have an easier afternoon this season as strode down Dalot’s flank to set up chance after chance. Every move seems half-hearted and lacked determination.

Harry Maguire – 5

Cut a frustrated figure as he debated with Martinez at times. Both Maguire and Martinez were left wide open on the counter by United’s midfield.

United shifted into Maguire up front territory the final embers. That’s how desperate their performance was.

Lisandro Martinez – 4

Scored a disastrous own goal as he should have booted the clearance away in a horror show at the back. Fittingly too, after being booed for his country’s antics at the World Cup.



Was denied by a brilliant Leno save after 10 minute, but was second best in battle with Fulham‘s summer signing Gonzalo Garcia and Josh King.

Luke Shaw – 5

Struggled on his return. When Fulham decided to give Dalot a rest, Fulham switched attention to the right hand side for King and Oscar Bobb to give Shaw the run around as he often came too narrow.

Youri Tielemans – 5

Too often outmuscled and outbid by Fulham’s midfield duo of Shea Charles and Sander Berge.

The 29-year-old lacks pace and struggles to press with intent. Made up for his slow half with a delicious through ball for Rashford.



Kobbie Mainoo – 6

The England midfielder oozes composure and was tidy on the ball again to continue the trend of being United’s best player this season.

The away end booed Mainoo’s substitution for Mason Mount with ten minutes left.

Bruno Fernandes – 5

The captain looks resigned. He hit the post and led United’s press as he so often does, but it left huge chunks of space behind him in the structure.



Fernandes has not got ticking this season yet, which is hurting United, who were over-run again.

Bryan Mbeumo – 5

The right side triangle of Mbeumo, Tielemans and Dalot left a lot to be desired. If Rashford was always criticised for his lack of defensive cover, it’s only right that Mbeumo’s is mentioned.

Marcus Rashford – 5

Started the afternoon as United’s most creative player across the opening matches, but the England star struggled to find his range, spurning two huge chances before the break.

Usually lethal on the counter, his passing were often underhit and wayward too. Hobbled around before he was replaced with 15 minutes on the clock. Disappointing and wasteful.



Matheus Cunha – 6

Improved after some poor performances. However, the strikerless system that worked last season should be retired. The Brazilian is not a No9 and looked frustrated out there.

Did well to dig it out from the byline to deliver a perfect ball for Fernandes’ effort that hit the post.

By no means perfect though as he should have been stronger when trying to claim a foul from Calvin Bassey in the lead up to 1-0.

Sports.title: Gary Neville is right as late equaliser at Fulham fails to spare lucky Man Utd blushes
Sports.content:
Gary Neville is right as late equaliser at Fulham fails to spare lucky Man Utd blushes

FULHAM 1-1 MANCHESTER UNITED: Matheus Cunha struck late to rescue a point for the Red Devils at Craven Cottage - but it didn't save them much embarrassment

View 3 Images Michael Carrick has plenty to ponder over the international break (Image: Luke Hastings/Wired Photos/Shutterstock)

How the mighty have fallen.

‌



Manchester United used to win games in Fergie time. Now they are left to snatch a lucky draw from the jaws of defeat.

‌



It spared them some embarrassment - but not much. Five games into the Premier League campaign, United are already 10 points behind Manchester City and another season is in danger of flatlining.

‌



United were so poor at times that Sky co-commentator Gary Neville called the performance “absolutely pathetic” and added: “I've watched United since the age of five. That's the worst 15 minutes I've seen them play.”

That might seem over the top. But let’s not forget that Neville is a club legend, former teammate of United boss Michael Carrick and his comments hit hard. They will resonate.

‌

They are also in keeping with a mood at a club which demands and expects better. The fans even turned on Carrick in the way they booed the substitution of Kobbie Mainoo at a time when they were chasing an equaliser.

Eventually, they got the leveller courtesy of Matheus Cunha’s deflected shot which was in keeping with their performance. It came after a big stroke of luck which was barely deserved.

‌



The goal at the other end which had put Fulham ahead came after Lisandro Martinez put through his own goal in real Keystone Cops fashion. It was laughably bad.

United desperately needed a win to lift the spirits and change the mood around Carrick going into a three-week international break. That will now feel painfully long.

View 3 Images Matheus Cunha's late deflected strike rescued a point for Manchester United at Fulham (Image: Getty Images)

‌



Sir Alex Ferguson was looking on from the posh seats and he must be wondering what on earth has gone wrong with United’s latest experiment.

Doesn’t this sound all too familiar? Club legend comes in to give United a lift, gets the desired effect and then - surprise, surprise - the next season is much harder to manage. This time it is Carrick and before it was Ole Gunnar Solskjaer.

It is happening again. And then, in the background, you have got joint United owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe making a fool of himself again.

‌



It was Ratcliffe making damning remarks about the country being “on the slide” in an interview about the Government failing businesses.

Honestly, for such an intelligent man his lack of self awareness is incredible. Talk about timing. You might want to get your own affairs in order first, Sir Jim. What a plonker.

But that is what United have come to. They spend millions, buy without much of a plan and leave themselves with a creaking defence marshalled by Harry Maguire who, at 33, showed his age as he lost his balance and crashed into a crate of bottles on the touchline.

‌



View 3 Images Lisandro Martinez put through his own goal to put Fulham ahead (Image: Getty Images)

Chasing after Fulham’s Josh King and Alex Iwobi must take it out of you. Fulham deserved more than a draw and the result at least takes them off the bottom and leaves Tottenham rock bottom going into the international break.

And that is the point. United’s first five fixtures - Hull, Ipswich, Everton, Manchester City and Fulham - was quite a friendly start. And they have blown it.

‌



Yes, they did OK first half as Bruno Fernandes hit the post and Cunha’s looping effort also hit the woodwork. But Fulham were good and are improving under Alvaro Arbeloa.

Fulham were the better team from the start of the second half. The opening goal came after 63 minutes. Calvin Bassey intercepted Mainoo’s loose pass, strode forward and his shot was parried by Senne Lammens only for Martinez to deflect the rebound into his own net.

Finally United showed some heart. They pushed forward in the closing stages and nicked a point in the last minute. Typical United. Cunha’s shot deflected off David Affengruber for an equaliser.

Sports.content:
Late Matheus Cunha goal rescues point for miserable Man Utd at Fulham - 5 talking points

FULHAM 1-1 MANCHESTER UNITED: The Red Devils head into the first international break of the window with just one Premier League win to their name following a disappointing draw at Craven Cottage

View 3 Images Matheus Cunha was the hero for Man United at Craven Cottage (Image: Getty Images)

Manchester United were rescued from another defeat by a late Matheus Cunha goal against Fulham.

‌



Michael Carrick's men struggled to find any rhythm in West London and fell behind as Lisandro Martinez put through his own net midway through the second half. Despite seemingly heading for defeat, Cunha popped up late on with a deflected effort to salvage a point.

‌



It leaves the Red Devils with just one win to their name and in the midst of their worst-ever Premier League start. Fulham in the meantime are still waiting for their first win under new boss Alvaro Arbeloa.

‌



Here are all of the talking points from Craven Cottage.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



Lammens saves United

Michael Carrick's side were indebted to their goalkeeper before the break, with Fulham having a number of opportunities to take the lead. Youngster Josh King had a couple of chances of his own, albeit saw good efforts saved by Senne Lammens.

Sander Berge also went close with a low effort that was parried by the Belgian. Alex Iwobi was also among the players to threaten United's goal throughout the first half as it lived a charmed life.

View 3 Images Senne Lammens was the only Man United star to leave Fulham with credit (Image: Getty Images)

‌



King continues to sparkle

Despite being just five games into the new campaign, this already looks like the season of Josh King at Craven Cottage. The Fulham academy graduate has established himself as a crucial player under Alvaro Arbeloa.

And his performance against United showed once more why he is so highly rated. King's movement is that of an elite ball carrier, while he was also a goal threat against the Red Devils.

He also showed the maturity of a senior player as he dictated instructions to his far more experienced teammates. King looks set to go to the very top.

‌



It's just a shame that he walked away with one blot on his copy book, that being a perceived dive towards the end of the first half.

Martinez mare

For all of Fulham's attacking verve, it was actually a United player that put through his own net to put the home side in the lead. The Red Devils failed to get the ball clear, with Matheus Cunha losing out.

Defender Calvin Bassey set his sights from range and saw his effort saved by Lammens. But the ball bounced back off Argentine defender Martinez and into the bottom corner.

‌



View 3 Images Lisandro Martinez was the guilty party at Craven Cottage (Image: Getty Images)

Cunha rescues United in Sesko absence

There was some bad news for United before the game with striker Benjamin Sesko ruled out through injury ahead of kick-off. And despite having not started a Premier League game this season, his absence was felt.

United lacked a focal point throughout the game, with Marcus Rashford and Bryan Mbeumo stationed out wide, while Cunha dropped deep. Not having Sesko on the bench also limited Carrick's options as he attempted to turn the game around.

‌



But to his credit, Cunha still managed to find enough space on the edge of the area to draw United level with his deflected effort.

United's rotten start goes on

Before the trip to Craven Cottage, United had endured their joint worst-ever start to a Premier League season. And despite having found an equaliser, it is still hugely disappointing.

The Red Devils were second best for large chunks of the game as they struggled to match their hosts' insensity and desire.

Article continues below

The draw leaves them 12th in the Premier League table with just five points from five games heading into the international break. It is certainly not the return United chiefs will have wanted after giving Michael Carrick the reins on a full-term basis. He has some questions to answer over the next few weeks.

Gary Neville was left astounded by the way Manchester United conceded against the Cottager and the ex-defender did not hold back on his thoughts

View 2 Images Gary Neville launched a stinging criticism of Manchester United (Image: Dennis Goodwin/ProSports/Shutterstock)

Gary Neville labelled Manchester United's start to the second half as "the worst 15 minutes I've ever seen" the club play. Fulham took the lead after half time in a goal strewn with errors by the Reds.

‌



It began with Matheus Cunha being easily dispossessed by Calvin Bassey, who drove forward with the ball and forced a save out of Senne Lammens. The Reds goalkeeper was then caught in two minds after Lisandro Martinez tapped the ball back to him.

‌



He seemingly could not decide whether to save the ball with his foot or with his hand and by the time he made up his mind, the ball was already in. After the goal was conceded, Neville tore into his former side while commentating for Sky Sports.

‌

He said: “I’ve watched Manchester United since the age of five and that’s the worst 15 minutes I’ve ever seen them play. Absolutely pathetic. They have walked for 15 minutes and you get what you deserve in a football match.”

When the camera panned to Michael Carrick, Neville added: "Maybe there will be a reaction but I've never seen a lack of effort for 15-20 minutes like I have just seen there. What must he be thinking? He probably cannot believe what he has watched in that last 15 or 20 minutes. He's got to act now."

‌



Neville most likely saw the goal coming as he was anything but impressed with how United started the second half. Before Martinez prodded the ball into his own net, Neville said: "It's a few minutes of the blue mannequins playing against the white mannequins and then it switches around, bizarre football match.

"They won't go anywhere with a lack of urgency like this. I don't know if it's fear, lack of complacency, they're just not working hard."

View 2 Images Martinez's own goal came after some poor United defend (Image: 2026 Getty Images)

‌



United did manage to get an equaliser through Matheus Cunha as the game headed towards the 90-minute mark. The Brazilian struck the ball from just outside the box and watched his effort deflect off David Affengruber and trickle past the wrong-footed Bernd Leno.

His fortuitous goal rescued the Reds from a third consecutive loss in all competitions. Carrick's side came into the match having lost to Manchester City last week and 3-2 to Brighton and Hove Albion in the League Cup.

After the match, former United ace Ashley Young tore into United, saying: "They were too slow. They were walking, they were jogging, there was not enough urgency in the game."

Sports.title: Longest serving manager in Scotland leaves after misconduct investigation
Sports.content:
Longest serving manager in Scotland leaves after misconduct investigation

Scottish side The Spartans have parted ways with manager Dougie Samuel after 14 years following a misconduct investigation this month

View 2 Images Douglas Samuel has left The Spartans (Image: Instagram/The Spartans)

The longest-serving manager in Scottish football has left his club following allegations of misconduct. Dougie Samuel has left The Spartans FC after 14 years at the helm.

‌



Earlier this month, it was announced that the 59-year-old would be taking a period of 'extended leave' from the club. Now, the Edinburgh-based club have confirmed that Samuel has departed following an 'independent investigation into allegations of misconduct'.

‌



Paul Thomson was made interim head coach following Samuel's initial leave of absence and is set to continue in that role. Former Hibernian and Kilmarnock manager Mixu Paatelainen, the side's sporting director, has assisted the coaching staff this month.

‌



Samuel had led the club since 2012 and helped them progress from the Lowland League into the SPFL three years ago.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

"Following an independent investigation into allegations of misconduct, The Spartans FC Head Coach Douglas Samuel has left the club," a club statement read.

‌



"Out of respect for the privacy of the individuals involved, and in accordance with our confidentiality policies, we will make no further comment on the specific details of the investigation or its findings

"Paul Thomson will continue as our Interim Head Coach for the foreseeable future, we really appreciate the commitment of our coaching, medical and support teams plus our players through this busy spell with another game on Tuesday."

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



Spartans currently sit third in the fourth tier of Scottish football following the opening eight matches of the season. They lost 3-0 at Dumbarton in their most recent match.

Earlier this year, Samuel reflected on his time at The Spartans as he approached 5,000 days at the club.

"Absolutely not!" he said when asked if he expected to stay at the club for 14 years. "I'm not somebody who sort of looks that far ahead in my life.

‌



"I've got goals and aspirations, but I try to live my life in the moment, in the present. It's very difficult, you know. I think the reality is that it's a part-time job in name, but certainly not in nature.

View 2 Images Douglas Samuel was successful at The Spartans in his 14-year spell (Image: Instagram/The Spartans)

"If you want to be a success at any level, you're thinking about it, you're working on it almost every day.

‌



"But I had a massive warning in my early 50s. I suffered a heart attack. I was doing two jobs full-time and I was probably doing too much.

"I was in a spin class. I fainted on my bike. I had a heart attack and my wife was on the bike next to me, so that was obviously quite a traumatic experience. But it’s probably one of the best things that ever happened to me - I was very lucky that it then revealed that I needed some treatment. I got a couple of stents fitted.

"It was a real wake-up call. I was very, very lucky and from that day onwards, I've tried to have a better balance and crucially keep perspective because I think sometimes we forget that it is the beautiful game, but it is a game.

Article continues below

"It's no life or death and I think it's important that we have perspective and that we try and enjoy the journey and enjoy the experiences.

"Of course, it matters a great deal to a great deal of people. But it is still a game and I think it's important to remember that at times. But I'm driven because life's about purpose as well. We try and leave a legacy."

Sports.title: Michael Carrick explains Benjamin Sesko absence vs Fulham as Man Utd suffer fresh blow
Sports.content:
Michael Carrick explains Benjamin Sesko absence vs Fulham as Man Utd suffer fresh blow

Benjamin Sesko didn't travel with the Manchester United squad for their Premier League clash with Fulham and Michael Carrick has confirmed the reason for his absence

View 2 Images Manchester United were without Benjamin Sesko at Fulham (Image: James Gill - Danehouse/Getty Images)

Manchester United are assessing Benjamin Sesko after the striker picked up an injury, Michael Carrick has confirmed. Sesko, 23, missed Sunday's clash with Fulham, having not travelled to London with the rest of Carrick's squad.

‌



The Slovenia international was subbed off in the second half of Wednesday's woeful 3-2 loss at home to Brighton in the Carabao Cup. It's possible that the setback is a reoccurrence of the shin injury which he first sustained during a clash with Liverpool in May and ruled him out of pre-season.

‌



When asked for an update before kick-off at Craven Cottage, Carrick replied: "A little bit of an assessment at the moment. He pulled up after the game the other day with a little bit of pain, so we'll have to see how he is."

‌



Sesko featured in United's first six matches of the season, starting two. He scored in games against Everton and Sabah.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



Sesko is now a doubt for his country's Nations League fixtures against Scotland, North Macedonia and Switzerland during the international break. The ex-RB Leipzig star was called up by Slovenia manager Bostjan Cesar earlier this week.

Carrick hoped to have Sesko at his disposal for what was billed as a must-win game, as Matheus Cunha started up front instead. After mustering just four points from their opening four Premier League games, the pressure was on the Red Devils boss.

"I know the club, I know the role, I know what's expected here in terms of playing at a certain standard, playing at a certain level, achieving certain things on the pitch," Carrick said.

‌



"In terms of future and ownership and how long I've got in the job, that's just totally not in my thinking, not one part of it. Like, how long I've got. It's ridiculous to think that way in a position that I'm in, that's just not on the radar.

Should Manchester United have signed a striker? Have your say in the comments section.

View 2 Images Michael Carrick needs results to ease the pressure on him (Image: Ash Donelon/Manchester United via Getty Images)

Article continues below

"I understand what we need to achieve and where we need to be as a football club for the owners, what they expect, for the supporters as much as anything… there's not [much] more important for me than what they expect and what they want to see. I get all that.

"It's two or three games that we haven't had certain results and two or three games too many because I really hate losing. But that doesn't mean that the world caves in. In some minds, it does. It can't for us because we've got to perform, we've got to get wins and we've got a lot of games to plan for. That's exactly what we're doing."

Sports.title: Premier League star announces international retirement moments after stunning display vs Arsenal
Sports.content:
Premier League star announces international retirement moments after stunning display vs Arsenal

Brighton star Pascal Gross was key during the Seagulls’ stunning 3-0 win against Arsenal on Saturday afternoon and confirmed that he had stepped back from international duty after the game

View 2 Images Gross was pivotal to Brighton's win against Arsenal (Image: Getty Images)

Brighton star Pascal Gross confirmed his Germany retirement just moments after leading the Seagulls to a memorable win against Arsenal. Fabian Hurzeler’s men secured a stunning 3-0 win with Gross, Charalampos Kostoulas and Chema Andres all on the scoresheet.

‌



Having also notched an assist for the defender’s goal, Gross extended his brilliant early season form. The 35-year-old now has four goals and four assists in just eight appearances in all competitions.

‌



Despite that form, Gross will not be earning a spot in Jurgen Klopp’s Germany squad, having confirmed that he has hung up his boots for the national side. "Officially – since I don't have social media – I haven't announced my retirement, but I have already retired," the 19-cap midfielder said to Sky Sports.

‌



"For me, it was over after the World Cup. I think it's time to wish the new generation nothing but the best and to keep my fingers crossed for them."

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



Gross only returned to Brighton from Borussia Dortmund in the summer and said that he is loving life back at his former home.

He added: "I thought we showed great intensity, waited for mistakes and punished Arsenal. It was a strong performance, a very complete performance.

"We won the ball high up and attacked really fast. After the last two wins we are full of confidence and wanted to finish really strong before the international break.

‌



View 2 Images Pascal Gross has been in stunning form this season (Image: Getty Images)

"I feel really good. I can't complain. I just try to help the team when I can. I really enjoy life in Brighton – I'm loving it.

"I know after the international break we play every three days and a lot of the lads are not used to that. It will be tough. I hope we can compete. We have a big squad this season."

Article continues below

Boss Hurzeler was also full of praise for Gross and his performance. Speaking about his star midfielder, he said: "We spoke about Pascal Gross and I said, I think in my last press conference, that you can compare him a little bit with a good wine. The older he gets, the better he is.

"He’s not only a player who makes his team-mates better, he’s not only a player who really understands the game so well. I think the things you can’t measure are the things we see in the daily business and on the training ground.”

Sports.title: Liverpool grind out Bournemouth win on Andoni Iraola's return - 5 talking points
Sports.content:
Liverpool grind out Bournemouth win on Andoni Iraola's return - 5 talking points

BOURNEMOUTH 0-1 LIVERPOOL: Andoni Iraola made a winning return to the Vitality Stadium courtesy of a second-half goal from Alexander Isak in a game of few chances

View 5 Images Alexander Isak's goal was enough for Liverpool (Image: Glyn KIRK/AFP via Getty Images)

Liverpool continued their unbeaten start to the season with a hard-fought 1-0 win away to Bournemouth. Alexander Isak's goal made the difference, breaking the deadlock just before the hour mark.

‌



Chances were few and far between on the south coast, with both teams seemingly sapped from a busy first portion of the season before the first international break.

‌



The game also marked Andoni Iraola's first visit back to Bournemouth since leaving the Cherries in May. His successor, Marco Rose, was looking for his first Premier League win, having started their Europa League campaign with a victory against Real Sociedad.

‌



Here are five talking points from the Vitality Stadium.

FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



1. Alisson's still got it

Thirty three is no age for a goalkeeper, but the injury which ruled Alisson out for two months at the end of last season raised questions over Liverpool's state of affairs between the posts. Giorgi Mamardashvili wasn't convincing when he deputised and fans were concerned when Alisson was linked with a move to Juventus over the summer.

The Brazilian was reportedly open to joining the Serie A giants, but fortunately for Liverpool, a deal never materialised. Alisson sent a reminder of his world-class ability in the 18th minute when he denied Evanlison from close range.

Marcus Tavernier blazed down the left flank and looked certain to continue his prolific run of form with an assist when Evanlison got the better of Virgil van Dijk and flicked his team-mate's cross towards goal. But Alisson got down brilliantly to tip the ball around the post for a corner, keeping it goalless.

‌



View 5 Images Alisson pulled off a superb save in the opening stages (Image: Glyn KIRK/AFP via Getty Images)

2. Not up to speed

Intensity. It was a core principle of Jurgen Klopp's football and is a buzzword for Andoni Iraola. It's also what Liverpool lack.

Judging by the first half, you'd suspect it was Liverpool who'd played away in Europe on Thursday night, not the other way around. The Reds' midfield of Alexis Mac Allister, Dominik Szoboszlai and Florian Wirtz was getting overrun, with Bournemouth playing as they did under Iraola for the last three seasons.

‌



Their decision to appoint Rose was made with the aim of continuing that style of play, whereas Liverpool are attempting to transition from Arne Slot's more controlled approach. It seems that the Spaniard needs more time.

Where will Liverpool finish this season? Give us your prediction in the comments section.

View 5 Images Marco Rose replaced Andoni Iraola at Bournemouth (Image: Catherine Ivill - AMA/Getty Images)

‌



3. Gakpo and Isak combine again

It's now four Premier League goals for Alexander Isak - all made by Cody Gakpo. Although the Dutchman didn't get the official assist this time, it was his driving run down the right wing which created the chance for Isak.

James Hill did his best to cut out the cross under pressure from Wirtz, but the Bournemouth defender couldn't get enough on it. The ball fell kindly to Isak, who made no mistake to break the deadlock.

The goal begged the question: where would Liverpool be this season without Gakpo? The 27-year-old's future was uncertain until the dying embers of the summer transfer window, with both Tottenham and Manchester City interested, and he's proving that he was worth keeping.

‌



View 5 Images Cody Gakpo was the provider for Alexander Isak again (Image: Mike Hewitt/Getty Images)

4. The Wirtz conundrum continues

Glance at the stats and you'd assume that Wirtz had a good game. His tally of three chances created was the joint-most in the match when Iraola subbed him off in the 73rd minute, and he played a part in Isak's goal.

But the Germany international had a difficult afternoon. Wirtz was particularly poor in the first half, squandering possession on several occasions.

‌



When the £116million man was replaced by Trey Nyoni, Jamie Carragher stated on commentary that he could have 'no complaints'. It's safe to say that the jury is still out.

View 5 Images Florian Wirtz flattered to deceive once more (Image: Catherine Ivill - AMA/Getty Images)

5. Wait goes on for Rose

It's now five games and no wins for Bournemouth in the Premier League. Although the Cherries made history in midweek, the reality is that the English top flight remains their bread and butter.

Article continues below

Hovering one place above the relegation zone - for now - things don't get much easier after the two-week international break. Bournemouth travel to Chelsea on October 10 to kick-off nine games in 27 days.

It's a period that will test Rose's squad which Justin Kluivert currently isn't a part of due to an injury which he suffered on Thursday. But it's also a chance to make more history.

Sports.title: Manager holds back tears on live TV as he's told about tragic death of his friend
Sports.content:
Manager holds back tears on live TV as he's told about tragic death of his friend

German football legends Peter Hermann died on Saturday and Niko Kovac was told of the death of his friend live on television following Borussia Dortmund's win over Stuttgart

View 2 Images Niko Kovac was clearly upset after being told about the death of a friend (Image: Sky Sports Germany)

Borussia Dortmund manager Niko Kovac was left distraught after he was informed of the death of his friend and colleague during a post-match interview on Sky Sports. Peter Hermann, Kovac's assistant at Bayern Munich, died following a battle with neurodegenerative illness, amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS), aged 74.

‌



Dortmund came away victors against Stuttgart, thanks to Maximillian Beier's goal, to continue their perfect record at the top of the Bundesliga. But Kovac was unable to hold onto the joy of another three points as the news of Hermann's passing broke while he was on the air on Saturday.

‌



Presenter Sebastian Hellmann received the news during an interview with Kovac and informed the Dortmund boss, in addition to pundits Lothar Matthaus and Julia Simic. Kovac was visibly upset by the news and said: “It leaves me a little short of breath.

‌



“One or two months ago I was still trying to speak to him, that was no longer possible at all. Unfortunately, his illness was incurable.

“I am deeply saddened, a good person has left us.”

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



While Kovac went on to cancel a media appearance with ZDF’s Aktuelles Sportstudio on Saturday evening. "We had actually planned to speak with BVB coach Niko Kovac at this point," explained presenter Katrin Müller-Hohenstein.

"However, he canceled at short notice because he had just learned of the death of his long-time colleague and assistant coach Peter Hermann,"

Kovac cut an emotional figure during his press conference. The Croatian had to fight back tears as he spoke about his friends death.

‌



View 2 Images Niko Kovac worked with Peter Hermann at Bayern Munich (Image: TF-Images/Getty Images)

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

“From me and also from my brother, our sincere condolences to Peter’s family," he said. “A great man has left us.

‌



“Not only as an assistant coach in Munich, but also as assistant coach when I was still a player in Leverkusen. Really a shock.”

Herman was a veteran of more than 1,000 matches as an assistant coach. The German spent time with Dortmund, Bayern Munich, FC Nuremberg, Schalke 04, Hamburg SV, Bayer Leverkusen and the Germany national team as he played a pivotal role at the highest level of German football.

Leverkusen paid tribute to their former coach with a glowing endorsement. "More renowned and respected in the sport than many a head coach," their tribute read.

‌



"An undisputed football expert, Hermann never made a fuss about himself. Down-to-earth, modest, loyal. A man with a great sense of humour and without a trace of vanity. A team player, a meticulous worker and a good listener."

Bayern were similarly effusive in the regard they hold Hermann. "Arm in arm with Franck Ribéry, deep in conversation with David Alaba, beer showers with Arjen Robben – there are countless scenes that have stayed in the memory and show what an extraordinary figure Bayern lost on Saturday," they said.

"Peter Hermann, the indispensable right-hand man of treble-winning boss Jupp Heynckes, passed away at the age of 74, and German football is mourning the loss of a unique bridge between generations, a man of great humanity and a true specialist in his field."

Sports.title: Ireland blow 19-point lead to lose to USA in WXV Global Series
Sports.content:
Freda Tafuna of the United States starred against Ireland

Ireland blew a 19-point lead to suffer a 40-36 loss to the USA in their opening game of the WXV Global Series.

The hosts romped to a 17-0 lead in the first 20 minutes in Dublin, with Vicky Elmes Kinlan opening the scoring and Dannah O'Brien scoring a conversion.

Tries from Cliodhna Moloney-MacDonald and Aoife Wafer made it 24-12 at half-time.

Early in the second half Ireland extended their advantage to 19 points, leading 31-12.

But the visitors, led by a player-of-the-match performance from Freda Tafuna, patiently clawed their way back into the clash with four successive tries from Kathryn Treder, twice, Hallie Taufoou and Tafuna.

Tafuna's try, scored while Kinlan was in the sin-bin, set the tone for the USA's first win over Ireland since 2018.

Scott Bemand's side are back in action next weekend away to Japan on Sunday at the Dexcom Stadium.

Sports.title: 'Might be time to wrap it up' - O'Neill to consider Celtic future
Sports.content:
Martin O'Neill will take stock as his future as Celtic boss comes under further scrutiny following the 1-0 defeat by Rangers at Parkhead.

The Light Blues cruised to a 3-0 League Cup win over the Hoops at Ibrox last Sunday and, in the Scottish Premiership rematch, a first-half strike by Ryan Naderi took Derek McInnes' side to within two points of the Hoops at the top of the table going into the international break.

In his second spell as permanent manager after two stints as interim boss last season, O'Neill was under growing pressure going into the game after the 3-1 loss to Ferencvaros at Parkhead on Thursday night.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Ryan Naderi fired Rangers to victory at Celtic Park

Following another poor performance, the 74-year-old spoke about entering a period of self-reflection.

"I genuinely will reflect and see," the Northern Irishman said. "It's a matter of whether I can help the team. The manager is supposed to be able to do that. I will look at that this week.

"I think every single time something crops up and things don't go so well, age plays a part. And, do you know what, they might be right. I'll be 110 in two years' time so it might be time to wrap it up.

"I will reflect on the games and speak to the board. You never know, they may well want to speak to me. I'll try to get a couple of days away and see how it goes."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player O'Neill felt the latest Old Firm defeat was a close game but he was shut down by former striker Chris Sutton who was left disappointed by the loss

Asked what would happen if he reflected, then decided he could not improve the team, O'Neill replied: "By that time, I will promise you, I'll let you know.

"I don't know. I'll have a look."

O'Neill addressed the growing negativity within the Hoops support, saying: "Well, I think they're absolutely entitled.

"I mentioned this to you on Friday, absolutely entitled to, of course.

"And I'm not immune from criticism. Far from it. Absolutely and utterly far from it.

"I think there's every reason to ask, 'can you turn this round? Can you change the whole thing?'

"We are, as I said, two points clear, so I have to kind of look at the bigger picture at this minute.

"But I knew that we were in a big, big fight anyway, with both ourselves, Rangers, and Hearts again, who are far from out of anything.

"It's a long season ahead. It's not the first time I've been questioned about my managerial time. So, yeah, I'll have a look at it. I will reflect and see."

'Celtic have big problems'

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Kris Boyd and Neil Lennon on Celtic's dismal display against Rangers

Former Celtic manager Neil Lennon on Sky Sports:

"He's [Martin O'Neill] changed formation, he made four changes midweek. He's trying to find a recipe to get some fluidity.

"Rangers were the far superior team, not just in physical attributes and running power, but football.

"They played all the football. Celtic were a lot better than they have been in the first half, without being brilliant.

"But second half, totally disjointed, totally outplayed. Outworked, which is the worst thing you can label at a team. Really disjointed, battered, actually battered.

"All the best players were in a blue shirt today. Celtic have a lot to ponder and a lot to work out.

"They've got an international break, which is probably coming at a good time for them. I know a lot of them may be away playing for their countries but there needs to be a total reset because the last three performances in the space of a week have been very poor."

Sky Sports' Chris Sutton:

"Knowing Martin, he'll be greatly concerned. I don't like to disagree with him but it wasn't a close game. There was a massive gulf between the teams.

"I can't actually remember a Celtic team getting such a doing at Celtic Park from a Rangers team, which happened today.

"It looked like Celtic were making it up as they went along. Rangers were better in every department.

"Celtic have got big problems. They were smashed by Rangers and that's a concern."

Sports.title: Heath bounces back after blowing lead to win first LET event
Sports.content:
England's Charlotte Heath secured her maiden Ladies European Tour title in dramatic fashion, holding off a host of challengers to claim victory at the La Sella Open in Denia, Alicante.

The 24-year-old rookie started the final round with a four-shot advantage and, despite seeing her lead disappear during a tense Sunday afternoon, she held her composure to card a final-round 73 and finish at 10 under par, two shots clear of the field.

After three weather-affected days, gusting winds continued to add an extra layer of difficulty, and set the stage for a thrilling finale at one of the LET's premier events.

Heath's front nine featured a solitary bogey at the fifth as she turned in 37, while Germany's Helen Briem mounted a strong challenge and briefly drew level at nine under par through 13 holes. However, Briem immediately dropped a shot at the next, allowing Heath to reclaim the outright lead.

As Briem and Shannon Tan of Singapore slipped back on the closing stretch, Italy's Alessandra Fanali posted the clubhouse target at eight under par.

The strongest challenge ultimately came from Englishwoman Alice Hewson, who surged into contention with a birdie finish. Standing over an eagle putt on the 18th that would have tied the lead, Hewson narrowly missed before tapping in for birdie, joining Fanali at eight under par.

Image: Heath bounced back after losing a four-shot lead before going on to win by two strokes

Heath was left needing a composed finish to seal the biggest victory of her career.

On the final hole, Heath split the fairway with her drive before finding a difficult position to the right of the green with her second shot. Unfazed, she pitched to nine feet and confidently rolled in a birdie putt to cap a remarkable week, ending her week with two birdies and two bogeys across the back nine.

The victory earns Heath her first LET title, a £128,722 (€150,000) winner's cheque and an unforgettable breakthrough moment in her rookie season.

"It's incredible," said Heath. "This year, I've gone out in the leading group twice before, so I guess it's third-time lucky.

"It was incredible having Alex [Long] on the bag. He kept me so calm and just reminded me that I'd played good golf all week. When the pressure is on, negative thoughts can creep in, so I'm very, very happy to get it done."

Heath admitted the mental challenge was as demanding as any shot she faced.

"You probably didn't want to be in my head on that golf course today," she said. "I was thinking I was going to shank it, hook it, pull it. You never know. Alex kept the ship steady all day."

Hewson, meanwhile, reflected on another strong performance at a venue she has long enjoyed.

Image: England's Alice Hewson finished tied for second at eight under par

"It's been a really solid week," she said. "I played some nice golf out there and probably didn't hole as many putts as I would have liked.

"La Sella is always one of my favourite stops on tour and having my whole family here made it even more special."

What's coming up next?

The LET travels to Italy for the Buccellati Ladies Italian Open at Golf Club Milano, which will be played from September 25-27.

Sports.title: McIlroy closes on Reed after BMW PGA near-miss | 'I had my chances!'
Sports.content:
Rory McIlroy has turned his attention to chasing down Patrick Reed for another Race to Dubai title after a cold putter cost him BMW PGA Championship victory.

McIlroy went into the final round two strokes back at Wentworth, where he recovered from failing to convert numerous birdie chances to briefly grab a share of the lead during a thrilling final round.

The world No 2 stumbled to a closing par to post a final-round 68 and finish in tied-second on 15 under, two strokes behind winner JJ Spaun, leaving McIlroy with a fourth runner-up finish at the DP World Tour's flagship event since his 2014 win.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the fourth round of the BMW PGA Championship, where JJ Spaun claimed an impressive victory

"I had my chances out there!" McIlroy told Sky Sports. "I felt like I hit the ball really well - probably the best I've hit it all week.

"Had good chances on two, three, five, eight, nine, 10, 13, the last. I felt like I hit good putts but, a bit like last week [Amgen Irish Open], I was just not seeing the lines that well.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player McIlroy birdied the seventh hole during his final round, following an incredible approach shot

"I struggled with some of the reads today and I hit some good putts that didn't go in. I holed a couple coming down the stretch but I think the story of the week was that I didn't hole as much as I should have.

"If I did, it would have been a different story."

Will Reed stop McIlroy's Race to Dubai title bid?

McIlroy ending in a four-way share of second earned him 532 Race to Dubai points and moved him within 308 of Reed, who withdrew mid-round on Friday due to injury, in the season-long standings.

Image: McIlroy finished two strokes behind Spaun after a dramatic Sunday at Wentworth

Reed had said he was looking forward to a battle with McIlroy, who will next feature at the DP World India Championship from October 15-18 before the two season-ending DP World Tour Play-Offs in the Middle East.

The Northern Irishman has topped the Order of Merit in four consecutive seasons and is looking to finish No 1 again, which would pull McIlroy level with Colin Montgomerie's all-time tally of eight Race to Dubai titles.

Image: Will McIlroy pull level with Colin Montgomerie this season?

"As soon as The Open was over, really that was the goal for the rest of the year," McIlroy added. "I would obviously love to do it [win the Race to Dubai].

"For Patrick, it was unfortunate this week. Hopefully he's okay and he can play what he needs to going in to really make it a good battle, but I'm excited.

"I'll keep working on my game over the next three weeks, then hopefully have a strong end to the season and give myself a great chance at that eighth one."

Image: McIlroy played alongside Adam Scott on the final day, who also finished in a share of second

'McIlroy missed putt after putt!'

McIlroy's runner-up finish at Wentworth follows previous seconds there in 2018, 2022 and 2024, leaving him still searching for his first worldwide win since successfully defending his Masters title in April.

"I think McIlroy left a little bit behind him on the greens - he had loads of chances," former Ryder Cup captain Paul McGinley told Sky Sports.

"It was surprising for a guy who has really improved his putting over the past couple of years and looks so good over them, but he seemed to miss putt after putt after putt.

Sports.title: Cunha's late deflected equaliser grabs Man Utd point at Fulham
Sports.content:
Matheus Cunha's deflected 89th-minute strike grabbed Manchester United a 1-1 draw at Fulham to take the edge off what appeared to be turning into a full-blown crisis for Michael Carrick's side going into the international break.

A horror-show own goal from Lisandro Martinez with 23 minutes to play piled the pressure on United to snatch something from this match, following the midweek Carabao Cup collapse at home to Brighton and Manchester derby defeat last weekend.

A wicked flick off David Affengruber got them out of jail. But United are still in the bottom half of the Premier League after five games, 10 points adrift of table-topping neighbours City and looking miles off the level required to challenge the country's best sides this season. This is their joint-worst start to a Premier League campaign.

A joint-worst start to a Premier League season for Man Utd Manchester United have won just five points from five league games this season – their joint-fewest at this stage of a Premier League campaign (also 5 in 2014-15).

"A real mess" was how Sky Sports' Gary Neville described the own goal. Cunha was levered off the ball by Fulham centre-back Calvin Bassey, whose stinging shot was parried by Senne Lammens. The 'keeper then saw Martinez stick out a boot and divert the ball back past him. Lammens' clumsy attempt to cut it out summed up United's chaotic defending.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Man Utd's Lisandro Martinez scored an unfortunate own goal as the ball bounced off him to give Fulham the lead

It was their play on the ball before that which most worried Neville, though. He called their passive possession before the opener "the worst 15 minutes I have ever seen Manchester United play".

The narrative could have been very different had Bruno Fernandes found the net rather than the post from Cunha's inviting cutback in the first half, or if the Brazilian's heavily deflected shot had gone in rather than clipped the woodwork. Bernd Leno also made a series of full-stretch saves.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Bruno Fernandes hits the woodwork for United

Eventually, the Fulham 'keeper was beaten, with no chance of stopping the leveller. It was heartbreak for the hosts and their new boss Alvaro Arbeloa who is still searching for his first Premier League win. He will take encouragement from this performance after their draw at Anfield, though, as they move off bottom spot by goal difference.

As for United, the accumulation of poor performances already this season will have alarm bells ringing in Manchester. They got away with a point at Fulham but have to find a way to make a major gear change during the upcoming three-week break to get back on track and realise their ambitions of kicking on this season.

Cunha: They put in more energy than us - we cannot accept this

Man Utd's Matheus Cunha to Sky Sports:

"It is so frustrating for us. In the beginning, we put the plan in and created some chances. We didn't score and then they scored in one action. It is hard to explain.

"It is frustrating for us. After the goal, we played much better and had a lot of character. It needs to be from the start. It is only one point but we should never play for one point.

"It is hard. They put in more energy than us, we cannot accept this. We need to do our best. We need to improve in every single position. It is only the beginning. Last season was the same, with noise around, but we finished third."

Carrick: We created enough to win the game

Man Utd boss Michael Carrick to Sky Sports:

"I thought we should've won the game, we created enough to win the game. We had a lot of good play and the goal we did concede, it is one of those goals.

"I really liked the reaction and how we finished the game. It would be easy for it to go in another direction.

"We nearly won it at the end. We came to get the win; of course we did, but the way we finished the game is the positive we take from it.

"Their goalkeeper, the saves he has made, he was player of the match and we hit the post twice. A lot of it [our play] was good. There are things to take from it, for sure."

Arbeloa: Every decision was for them

Fulham boss Alvaro Arbeloa to Sky Sports:

"We were so close. So, so close. We were a little bit unlucky again. We knew it would be difficult against this big team.

"Also we knew what happened last week. We have seen what the referees have been doing in all the matches so it was a difficult game. And we were unlucky.

"All fouls for them. You can see before they scored, the foul against Maguire, it's a guy who is 100 kilos. Every decision was for them and I knew after the game against Man City that they [would not] let Manchester United lose here. We deserved a little bit more."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Fulham boss Alvaro Arbeloa said there were key decisions that did not go his side's way, and felt the referee 'didn't like' to let Manchester United lose

In his press conference, Arbeloa appeared to row back on his comments a little bit - but still said he "was not really happy".

"My English is not so good," he said. "Maybe I explain myself so bad and I prefer not to say anything about the referees because you never know.

"When you say something that you don't have to say, it's better to stay calm, focus on the performance of my team and focus on the next game.

"I'm not really happy. Like I said, I need to be focused and put my energy in all the things that I have to improve.

"[Maguire] is a very big guy and maybe it wasn't a foul. But it's ok. Like I said, I prefer to analyse the game - players, systems and it's the best for win.

"You know when you draw a game like that, maybe you're a little bit frustrated."

The key moments from Craven Cottage

10: SAVE! Martinez flies a shot from just outside the Fulham box towards the top-corner after a half-cleared cross - but Leno stretches to push it away.

25: POST! Cunha gets around Affengruber and cuts the ball back but Fernandes steers his shot against the far post.

28: SAVE! Lammens saves Josh King's volley from close quarters when the youngster meets Alex Iwobi's cross.

31: CHANCES! Gonzalo Garcia miscues a volley and Sander Berge has his follow-up shot well saved by Lammens before Oscar Bobb drags wide from another good position for Fulham.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Cunha's shot on goal hits the post after a slight deflection

31: POST! A big deflection loops Cunha's shot over Leno and against the far post, with the ball coming back off the 'keeper and out for a corner.

32: SAVE! Lammens is forced into another good stop, sticking out a leg to keep out King's strike.

63: OWN GOAL! After a sleepy start to the second half, Bassey overpowers Cunha and fires a shot which Lammens parries - and is bundled back past him by Martinez

67: SAVE! Leno stretches to save Bryan Mbeumo's curling shot.

74: SAVE! Leno again at full stretch to deny Cunha.

86: PENALTY APPEALS! Man Utd want a penalty for handball from Bassey after Martinez turns the ball against him. But his arms are tucked into his body.

89: GOAL! Cunha's deflected shot grabs United a last-gasp equaliser.

Sports.title: Palace secure valuable point at unbeaten Leeds
Sports.content:
Crystal Palace secured a useful point at in-form and unbeaten Leeds as Pierre Sage's side produced a much-improved defensive display to hold the hosts to a goalless draw at Elland Road.

The stalemate was enough to lift Sage's side one point clear of the relegation zone heading into the three-week international break.

Palace arrived having conceded 11 goals in their opening four Premier League games but, after a cagey first half, grew into the contest and were the more threatening side after the break. Tyrick Mitchell had the ball in the net only for it to be ruled out for offside.

Leeds, unbeaten coming into the game after an impressive 4-1 win over Newcastle, struggled to reproduce that attacking fluency. Dominic Calvert-Lewin, who had scored in each of his previous five Premier League home games, was largely starved of service, eventually being denied by Walter Benitez after the break.

Palace had chances to snatch it late on, with Adam Wharton continuing to influence proceedings and Eddie Nketiah and Ismaila Sarr combining for an opening that Tarik Muharemovic brilliantly recovered to stop. Leeds threw on attacking reinforcements and switched shape, but could not find the breakthrough.

For Palace, after conceding two or more goals in each of their previous 10 Premier League matches, they finally kept a clean sheet - and did so against a Leeds side that had scored 12 goals across their previous five home league games. The performance gives Sage a platform to build on after a difficult opening month.

The key moments from Elland Road

10: SMART TACKLE! Muharemovic makes a crucial intervention to deny Jorgen Strand Larsen after Quinten Timber had slipped the Palace striker through on goal.

22: OVER! Ao Tanaka fires over from close range after Leeds' long throw caused problems in the Palace box.

31: PALACE PUSHING! Strand Larsen, Timber and Wharton all see efforts blocked as Palace threaten to break the deadlock.

53: OFFSIDE, NO GOAL! Mitchell fires Palace in front after Anan Khalaili's cross, but VAR confirms Khalaili was offside in the build-up.

57: WHAT A SAVE! Benitez produces an excellent reaction stop to deny Calvert-Lewin after James Justin's cross picked out the in-form striker.

71: PENALTY APPEAL! Daichi Kamada goes down under pressure from Ethan Ampadu, but the referee waves away Palace's claims.

83: BIG CHANCE! Wharton's clever ball releases Sarr into the area, but Justin recovers brilliantly to deny the Palace substitute.

88: PALACE OPPORTUNITY! Nketiah breaks clear after being played in by Wharton but chooses to square for Sarr, allowing Muharemovic to make a crucial recovery.

Palace showed exactly what they had been missing

Analysis by Sky Sports' William Bitibiri:

Crystal Palace arrived at Elland Road with 11 goals conceded from their opening four Premier League games. They leave with a clean sheet and, on balance in the second half, will probably feel they could have taken all three points.

This was a spirited, disciplined performance from Palace. They came out after the break with a completely different mindset and put Leeds under pressure.

Leeds were strangely flat. Calvert-Lewin was starved of service for long periods and even when the chances did arrive, Palace goalkeeper Benitez was there to deny him.

In the end, 0-0 feels like a reflection of two sides who cancelled each other out, but Palace can take far more encouragement from this performance than Leeds can.

For Sage, though, this is the sort of defensive display he will hope can become the foundation of a turnaround.

Farke: It was important to extend the unbeaten run

Leeds boss Daniel Farke speaking to Sky Sports:



"You're always just 100 per cent happy once you win the game, and of course, we wanted after our nearly perfect start to win this home game. Football-wise, it was not our best performance, but we also played against a well structured side.

"I think we were a bit too loose with the ball today, and in the execution in the opponent's half, in the final third.

"Our defending behaviour for 60 minutes was excellent. We took more risks and it was a more open game, a bit like a basketball game in the end.

"It also felt that they could perhaps win it in the end. It was one of those days when you don't have your best performance-wise, but then you have to dig in and fight.

"It was also important to keep the clean sheet and extend the unbeaten run, and for that we take this point."

Sage: Palace deserved more than a point

Crystal Palace boss Pierre Sage speaking to Sky Sports:

"We worked a lot during the last week on this, and we tested on our game on Thursday, but I think it was better and better. We conceded less chances than before. We conceded a big one, and our keeper made a big save. So I have to congratulate Walter Benitez for that.

"But at the end, during the game, not only the defensive part, but I think we deserve better."

On whether Palace deserved to win:

"Yes, I think because we create some chances and without scoring, the one that was cancelled by the VAR is normal because there's an offside. But it's a little bit frustrating because I think the players gave a lot in this game, and at the end they deserve something else than a draw."

On the fine margins:

"Yes, and I think we will speak about that in the future because one time is good, but we have to do it more."

Robinson: Neither side lost points - both gained one

Paul Robinson on Sky Sports:

"I thought Palace were excellent after the break.

"Both goalkeepers had to make excellent saves, but we were limited to few goalscoring chances. We witnessed two sides cancelling each other out.

"Neither side has lost points, but have gained one."

Sports.title: Spaun wins BMW PGA Championship as McIlroy falters despite late surge
Sports.content:
JJ Spaun outlasted a packed leaderboard of players on Sunday at the BMW PGA Championship, as the American capitalised on a stumble from Spain's Manuel Elvira to win his debut title at Wentworth.

An utterly thrilling final round of golf unfolded, with multiple players, including Rory McIlroy, Aaron Rai and Elvira, racing to the finish line, but all struggled to pull away from the pack.

There was heartbreak for Elvira, who had the chance to leapfrog Spaun at the top of the leaderboard after tying the 2025 US Open champion with an eagle on the 17th hole.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Spaun said he had a point to prove this week after being omitted from Brandt Snedeker's Presidents Cup team

With Spaun already in the clubhouse at 17 under, the Spaniard, who is ranked 294th in the Official World Golf Rankings, needed a birdie on the 18th to win his first DP World Tour title, but he stumbled, finding a fairway bunker with his tee shot before sending his bunker shot well past the green.

He attempted to chip back on but agonisingly sent his shot into another bunker before ultimately confirming Spaun's two-stroke win with a double-bogey.

Elvira would tie McIlroy, Rai and Adam Scott at 15 under par for second place, as 13 players would finish within three shots of the lead.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Manuel Elvira heartbreakingly carded a double-bogey on the final hole of the tournament to confirm Spaun's victory

McIlroy mixed in moments of brilliance with a few critical errors. The Northern Irishman also struggled to make birdie putts, but surged in his back nine, making birdies on holes 12, 14 and 17, to post a final-round score of 68.

Rai, who had taken the joint-lead after the first round, was impressive throughout his week at Wentworth, and the Englishman once again put the gas on as he tried to pull away from the chasing pack of players, taking the clubhouse lead before Spaun with a final-round 66.

Open champion Ryan Fox would join Matt Fitzpatrick, Joost Luiten and Filippo Celli tied for sixth place at 14 under.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Rory McIlroy showcased moments of brilliance but ultimately came up short on Sunday at Wentworth

Spaun, who was omitted from Brandt Snedeker's Team USA Presidents Cup squad, felt he had "taken care of business this week", showing his patience to bounce back from an early bogey on the first to card six birdies, and end with a score of 67.

"We [him and captain Brandt Snedeker] haven't spoken," the 36-year-old said. "But yeah, I played with a huge chip on my shoulder.

"I'm so delighted to be here and just play this event. I've always wanted to do this. The extra motivation, I think that is the willpower that you kind of have, determination.

"Being left off the Presidents Cup team a couple of weeks ago was very disappointing and I wanted to prove that I deserved to be on that team.

"I took care of my business this week, so all the best to my mates next week at Medinah, but I'll be on the couch watching."

Elvira 'devastated, but buoyed by performance

Image: Elvira cut a dejected figure after he made double-bogey on the 18th hole to finish in joint-second place

Elvira crouched down in frustration after missing his first putt on the 18th, cutting a shattered figure before eventually holing out for a double-bogey.

Despite coming up short, the Spaniard explained he was chuffed with his performance.

"Devastating that I hit the wrong shot at the right time on the lay-up and left myself the toughest shot in the fairway bunker, and I wasn't able to pull it off," he said.

"I've played some of the best golf, probably, of my life. I was in contention and I wasn't really that nervous. It's been a great week and I'm really glad for it."

McIlroy: I wish I had some of those putts back

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player McIlroy reflects on his final round at the BMW PGA Championship

After struggling to make an impact on the front nine, McIlroy found trouble on the 12th before producing an epic recovery shot around a cluster of trees, eventually going on to make birdie.

It was the spark the Northern Irishman needed, as he followed it with further birdies on the 14th and 17th. He came undone on the 18th, however, finding a fairway bunker before missing a putt for birdie.

"I wish I had some of those putts back," McIlroy said on his putting woes.

"But I have to be encouraged with where my game is at.

"Hit the ball really well. Hit the best I hit it during the course of the week and am encouraged with the signs that my game is going and just have to keep working at it."

What's next?

The next DP World Tour event is the FedEx Open de France, which gets under way on Thursday at Le Golf National, the venue for Europe's 2018 Ryder Cup triumph.

Meanwhile, Team USA will chase a record-extending 11th consecutive victory over the International Team at the Presidents Cup, which also begins on Thursday at Medinah Country Club in Illinois.

Sports.title: Littler's bid for major clean sweep ended by crushing Clayton defeat
Sports.content:
Luke Littler's bid for a clean sweep of all major PDC titles in 2026 is over after a crushing 10-4 defeat to Jonny Clayton in the last eight at the World Series of Darts Finals in Amsterdam.

The world No 1 had won the first six premier events of the season after following his World Championship triumph at Alexandra Palace in January with the World Masters, UK Open, Premier League, World Cup of Darts and World Matchplay.

Littler was hoping to add the World Series of Darts Finals, World Grand Prix, European Championship, Grand Slam of Darts and Players Championship Finals trophies to complete a historic monopoly over the year - but ran into an inspired Clayton, who reeled off seven of the last eight legs from 3-3.

Clayton will take on fellow Welshman Gerwyn Price in Sunday's second semi-final, after England's Ross Smith meets home favourite Gian van Veen in the first semi-final, with the final to follow.

What next for Littler?

Littler can still sweep the ranking events in 2026 - the World Series Finals, like the World Cup and Premier League, is non-ranked - if he wins the remaining four majors in Leicester, Dortmund, Wolverhampton and Minehead this autumn.

'The Nuke' has work to do to reach the Players Championship Finals, though, as he sits 125th on the Order of Merit in that series with six events of the regular season remaining and only the top 64 players advance to the finale in Somerset from November 27-29.

Clayton: Not the Littler we know but I took my chances

Jonny Clayton to ITV4 after victory over Luke Littler:

"To be honest, I just thought: 'Relax, go out and try your best.'

"What a player he [Littler] is. He wasn't full flow today, but you have to take your chances.

"Luke missed a lot of darts at doubles, and that's the name of the game. You have to take your chances. I did that and it's brilliant.

"The last dart in a double hurts, and it puts pressure on a player.

"All respect to Luke, he's fantastic but he gave me chances upon chances, and that's not the Littler we all know. But Jonny Clayton can play darts as well."

Van Barneveld: Everyone is fallible - Littler felt the pressure!

Raymond van Barneveld to ITV4:

"It's the pressure. Everyone talks about: 'Can he do the whole year and win all the big majors.' It gives big pressure. He wants to perform.

"He's the best player at the moment, but everyone is fallible. Everyone wants your scalp, and Jonny Clayton did it perfectly.

"In all honestly, Littler missed some crucial shots.

Image: Littler's performance was purely down to 'pressure', according to Raymond van Barneveld

Littler latest big name to exit in Amsterdam

Victory at the World Series of Darts Finals would have been Littler's second in three years, having beaten Michael Smith to triumph in 2024 before losing to Michael van Gerwen in the final 12 months ago.

Littler had suffered scares earlier this week, rallying from 3-1 down to defeat Danny Noppert 6-4 in round one and then surviving a last-leg shoot-out versus Nathan Aspinall to win 10-9 in the last 16.

World No 2 Luke Humphries was eliminated by Dirk van Duijvenbode in round two on Saturday, while defending champion Van Gerwen fell in the opening round on Thursday, losing to Daryl Gurney.

Van Gerwen's World Series Finals victory last season is the only major he has won since 2023 and he has failed to reach an individual quarter-final in this year's majors.

The 37-year-old did make it to the final of the World Cup of Darts for Netherlands alongside doubles partner Van Veen, where the Dutch duo were beaten by England's Littler and Humphries.

That World Cup victory for Littler in Frankfurt in June means the European Championship is the only major title absent from his CV - something he will hope to rectify in Dortmund next month.

Sports.title: Cunha strikes late to deny Fulham and salvage point for Manchester United
Sports.content:
To paraphrase a former Manchester United manager, Michael Carrick knew that the storm would come. Everything went a little too perfectly for him in the second half of last season. There would be ill winds at some point. Which was what Carrick could feel before this visit to Fulham. What were his emotions afterwards?

Relief was surely the main thing. Because after the derby defeat by Manchester City last Sunday and the midweek Carabao Cup exit against Brighton – both at Old Trafford – Carrick was starring at an unwanted hat-trick. All this on the back of other wobbles since the opening weekend when United lost at Hull. It is all extremely angsty and edgy.

It was a darkly comic own goal by Lisandro Martínez that raised Fulham’s hopes of a first Premier League win under Álvaro Arbeloa; an episode in which the United goalkeeper, Senne Lammens, emerged with zero credit. Put it down as a colossal mess. United have almost always won in this corner of south-west London in recent seasons. A crash against the team that started the day at the foot of the table was unthinkable.

Carrick and his team averted disaster when they caught a huge break with time almost up. There was little on for Matheus Cunha on the edge of the area, to the left of centre, and so he took on the shot for the near corner. The Fulham goalkeeper, Bernd Leno, looked to have it covered. Cue an almighty deflection off David Affengruber that sent the ball spinning into the opposite corner. United escaped.

It was true that Fulham invited pressure after the own goal. They sank back and came to lack an out-ball. But it did not look as though United would find the required moment. Carrick’s players were too slow. Their moves were predictable. They could not get in behind in the second-half, their only efforts coming from outside the area. Thankfully for Carrick, Cunha got one to work.

There was plenty to like about Fulham, who remain a work in progress under Arbeloa. He appears to have concluded that he needs greater security in central midfield – hence Sander Berge and Shea Charles, with Alex Iwobi moved out to the left wing. There were round pegs in round holes for Fulham, which was not completely the case for United, albeit they were able to welcome back Luke Shaw on the left side of their defence.

With no Benjamin Sesko because of a recurrence of his shin issue, Carrick was without his only pure No 9. His solution, once again, was to use Cunha as a false 9 and ask Bruno Fernandes to play close to him. It was a box midfield, with Youri Tielemans and Kobbie Mainoo further back. Arbeloa got his wingers, Oscar Bobb and Iwobi, to come inside to good effect. The battle for control of the middle of the pitch pulsed, with Josh King a major part of it.

The Fulham No 10 threatened during a first-half in which Fulham were the more urgent and creative team. King worked Lammens in the 32nd minute after buying a yard of space from Shaw and it was not the only time that United felt their hearts skip.

View image in fullscreen Lisandro Martínez and Senne Lammens rue handing Fulham the lead. Photograph: Peter Cziborra/Action Images/Reuters

Fulham had to be annoyed that they did not score before the interval. Twice, Gonzalo García fluffed his finish when well placed; on the second occasion, Berge extended Lammens on the second phase of the move. There was also the moment when Bobb spun into a seam of space only to drag wide. King wanted a free-kick on the edge of the area in the 45th minute after running into Harry Maguire but he was looking for the contact and was correctly booked for diving.
