United hit the woodwork twice in the first half and had other flickers. They got into some good positions only to lack composure. Cunha did well to wriggle clear of Affengruber on the right and pull back for Fernandes who flicked against the far post. Cunha also saw his first deflected shot of the day loop high and drop down against the outside of the upright. Martínez forced Leno into a decent save early on. Marcus Rashford lifted a good chance high.

United lost their way after the restart. They lacked energy and could get nothing going. It was as if they hit a wall and then came the gut punch of the own goal. It started when Cunha failed to hold up the ball in a deep midfield position. He was out-muscled by Calvin Bassey, who simply wanted it more. The Fulham captain pushed on to the edge of the area and when he unloaded, United’s problems were about to deepen.

Lammens’s parry was unconvincing and Martínez was ponderous. He could not set his feet properly and merely jabbed the ball towards his own goal. Whereupon Lammens, perhaps wondering whether it was a back pass, tried to clear with his feet and got it all wrong.

United could feel the red panic lights flashing. They fought to stabilise and the plus point for Carrick was that his players kept going. Bryan Mbeumo and Cunha forced Leno into fine saves with curlers from distance. The key point was that they were from distance. Fulham looked set to keep United at bay; they also went close to a second goal when Kevin, on as a substitute, forced Lammens into a save. Enter Cunha. He was the United saviour. The fault-lines for his team remain pronounced.

Sports.title: Semenyo helps chaotic Manchester City beat Sunderland despite Brobbey hat-trick
Sports.content:
Manchester City sent a message to Arsenal with this chaotic victory that takes Enzo Maresca’s team three points clear as leaders during the three-week international break.

Until the Premier League resumes on 10 October City can enjoy their status while Mikel Arteta’s champions have to stew following Saturday’s 3-0 humbling at Brighton.

Maresca will review this match because City lacked control and may not have enjoyed a 5-3 win that featured two Antoine Semenyo strikes for them, a Brian Brobbey hat-trick for Sunderland, with Enzo Fernández, Rayan Cherki and Erling Haaland the other scorers.

Maresca’s side are entertaining for the neutral and heart-palpitating for the manager. When the normally calm Rúben Dias hit the ball towards his goal and scrambled to hoof off the line, this was City in microcosm, versus Régis Le Bris’ potent visitors. The conclusion, though, from the season opening phase is that City will compete with the Gunners to the end of the title race – providing they become less fragile.

Sunderland conceded first by allowing a break at a corner that ended in Dayann Methalie chopping down Iliman Ndiaye. Next came a moment of Fernández skill from a free-kick along the right-hand edge of the box. City’s £125m deadline-day acquisition from Chelsea asked Ndiaye to alter position in the area, then guided the ball straight home, on the near side, his instruction to the winger hoodwinking Robin Roefs, Sunderland’s goalkeeper, who ended up on his backside. It was a first goal for Fernández since his equaliser in the World Cup semi-final for Argentina against England.

Having been excellent, City fell asleep seconds later. Enzo Le Fée is one of Sunderland’s star acts and the pinpoint pass into Brobbey that split Dias and Matheus Nunes showed why. The No 9’s first touch was smart, allowing him to then beat, with the outside of his right boot, the onrushing Gianluigi Donnarumma.

Maresca had billed the contest as City’s toughest so far and you saw now that this was not regulation respectful manager-speak. Le Bris’ side pinged the ball about and were quick to fire it into the danger area. Yet, when feeling too comfortable while playing out from the back, City pounced again. Kevin Danso’s loose pass from his area was nabbed by Ndiaye and the ball went instantly to Haaland near the penalty spot. Semenyo took over, tapped to Cherki and the Frenchman made space and threaded in.

That made it 2-1 to City with half an hour gone. Three minutes later a breathless opening period had another twist. Le Fée slipped in Thomas Meunier, the wide right forward crossed, and Brobbey could not miss. Following a prolonged video assistant referee check Sunderland’s second stood: Brobbey and Meunier being offside was the question and it appeared marginal.

Again, Maresca’s side suffered due to naivety. And, again, they roved upfield and breached their visitors’ rearguard. This time Cherki hit Marc Guéhi with a chip from the right that provoked a scramble in Sunderland’s area. The ball came out to Semenyo who powered in to restore City’s lead.

By the interval it should have been 4-2 but the normally lethal Haaland splayed wide after Ndiaye teed him up. The last bit of action had a mis-hit Brobbey effort nearly chipping Donnarumma who needed his 6ft 5in to tip over.

Maresca wanted the match slowed down in the second half, with the ball at City feet. Yet still holes were punched in them as when Elliot Anderson was caught upfield and Noah Sadiki ran into space and ballooned over.

View image in fullscreen Brian Brobbey gets to take the match ball home but the Sunderland striker looks dejected after the defeat. Photograph: Matt West/Shutterstock

Another goal looked to be needed because Sunderland were relentless. Cherki’s curving pass right to Ndiaye created a chance for the fourth but the winger’s touch was clumsy. Better was Semenyo’s decisiveness that made it 4-2. Cherki’s pass caused Nordi Mukiele a problem, the ball went to City’s Ghanaian international, and he arrowed into the far right corner.

Could City breathe? No was the answer. Anderson may have been lucky not to concede a penalty when the ball struck a hand in the area – another indication of City’s scruffiness: afterwards Le Bris stated this should have been a penalty, and you could see why.

Brobbey’s third arrived when Granit Xhaka delivered from the right, Nilson Angulo helped the ball on, and the Dutchman converted. This was seven goals before the hour mark in what was a basketball-like affair packed with incident that, next, included Haaland’s late fifth.

Jérémy Doku, on for Ndiaye, had Josko Gvardiol slaloming along the left, the defender’s cross to the far post slid beyond Roefs by the Norwegian. Initially flagged as offside, the VAR overturned the assistant referee’s call and that was 5-3 – the end of the scoring on an afternoon that will not be forgotten soon.

“Collectively we did what we could, fought together and got the three points,” Semenyo said. It also made it five wins from five for last season’s runners-up who, for now, are back in the box seat.

Sports.title: Isak pounces to give Liverpool victory on Iraola’s return to Bournemouth
Sports.content:
At the final whistle, victory secured, Andoni Iraola embraced both his current players and those he guided to new heights at Bournemouth last season. Liverpool are not yet the overwhelming, suffocating force Iraola wants them to become but they did enough to claim three points here, Alexander Isak capping a peculiar performance with a simple finish.

Cody Gakpo was again the architect, the Dutchman the supplier for all four of Isak’s goals this season. Isak’s only other shot before scoring was to balloon a first-time effort high and wide but his second-half strike was sufficient to return Liverpool to winning ways in the Premier League.

Perhaps it was inevitable that these teams would neutralise each other. On Iraola’s final day at Bournemouth’s training base he spent an hour in the company of his successor, Marco Rose, who is yet to taste victory in the Premier League. The pair stopped talking only because Tiago Pinto, Bournemouth’s sporting director, interrupted to remind them there were other things on the agenda.

“We knew what we were going to get, they knew what they were going to get and maybe you could see it,” Rose said. “It is mostly the same after our games; I sit here after a good performance, but you don’t get points for good performances. You have to force wins.”

Amine Adli, sidelined because of a calf injury, scored a 95th-minute winner in a 3-2 victory for Bournemouth in this fixture last season but there was no such chaos to this game. The only clear sight of goal arrived approaching the hour when Gakpo bypassed Adrien Truffert down the right flank and squared, the ball trickling towards Isak on the edge of the six-yard box.

A few minutes earlier Isak had sent Iraola retreating to the away dugout. “Yes, yes,” Iraola said, encouraging Isak as the Sweden striker made tracks on the wing, white shirts attacking the box, only for his wayward cross to end up with the ball flying towards the scaffolding structure in a corner of this ground, part of Bournemouth’s ongoing stadium upgrade.

View image in fullscreen Andoni Iraola applauds the fans after victory at the Vitality Stadium. Photograph: Ian Walton/AP

In midweek, Iraola was rooting for his former club on their European bow but promised a businesslike return to Bournemouth and stepped off one of the two Liverpool team coaches with a game face. Tommy Elphick, who captained Bournemouth to the Premier League in 2015 and followed Iraola to Liverpool, embraced old colleagues pitchside before the warm-up.

“I love it because I love this club and it is growing,” Iraola said after Liverpool extended their unbeaten start to seven games in all competitions. “They will enjoy European nights here. This stadium will become a lot nicer. I was delighted to see a lot of the people I appreciate so much.”

All the niceties, Iraola said, could wait until afterwards. Pablo de la Torre, his fitness coach who was part of his Bournemouth staff, made that clear within the opening 30 seconds, wresting the ball away from Adam Smith to delay the hosts taking a quick throw‑in. Bournemouth were intent on building on their history‑making win on Thursday in the Basque Country and had the best chance of the first half, Alisson’s smart right-hand save preventing Evanilson’s front-post flick squeezing in at his near post.

Dominik Szoboszlai dropped a typically vicious free-kick wide of Djordje Petrovic’s post and Petrovic saved a deflected Bradley Barcola shot, but Liverpool spent much of the first half containing Bournemouth’s threats. Iraola conceded that his side were slow out of the blocks.

“We didn’t start with the intensity that is required to win here,” he said. “You never play comfortably here – Bournemouth put you under pressure and you have to adapt.”

Liverpool only teased glimpses of quality. Florian Wirtz saw a disguised pass for Isak cut out and Bournemouth flew forward, the alert and again impressive Jérémy Jacquet extinguishing the danger as Ryan Christie flung his body to connect with a low cross. Christie chopped inside Szoboszlai close to the touchline and Scott switched play with a pinged diagonal pass.

Bournemouth seemed to be growing in confidence but then Gakpo breezed past Truffert, usually such a dependable performer who last week was given a France recall. Gakpo crossed from the right and while James Hill dived in to stop the threat of Wirtz at the front post, the ball dropped to an unmarked Isak on the edge of the six‑yard box to stroke the ball in.

It was not a nerveless finale. Iraola hopped on the touchline as Scott, poised to make his England debut in this international window, lined up a 90th-minute free‑kick. After Liverpool won a free-kick deep into four minutes of stoppage time, Iraola crossed his hands and frantically pointed his players towards the scoreboard showing there were only a matter of seconds remaining. Moments later, it was a case of job done. “I think in life you always get what you deserve,” a phlegmatic Rose said. “One error is too much, that’s the point.”

Sports.title: Rangers and Ryan Naderi finish off Celtic’s horror week with Old Firm victory
Sports.content:
If ever a stadium can be rocked by silence, this was the moment. With no visiting fans allowed at any of this season’s Glasgow derbies, Ryan Naderi’s winning goal was met with nothing but the banging of fists of the clear plastic of the Rangers bench, and the shouting of the broadcast commentators. A screaming void of apathy and atrophy, the sound of a beckoning abyss, of a title race blowing open and a team slowly breaking apart.

That Rangers were unable to celebrate this triumph with their fans in the stadium was, of course, a source of lament, as well as a measure of just how ugly this fixture has become over the years.

It has become a day that is no longer relished but dreaded, a failure not just of the two fanbases themselves but the authorities who have allowed the ugliness to fester, who have talked a tough game on sectarianism but done little in practice to combat it at source.

But nothing could spoil the mood of Derek McInnes’s team, humming after a tough start to the season and now able to toast a second victory over their rivals in the space of a week. For Celtic, sitting on three straight defeats, the silence will be filled with plenty of noises and voices over the coming international break: awkward questions and painful decisions that last season’s dramatic double may have forestalled but which can no longer be avoided.

The drop in standards over the opening weeks of this season has been alarming, and at 74 years of age Martin O’Neill is wise enough and self-aware enough to know that he may be as much part of the problem as part of the solution. For him, the next few weeks will be a time of “self-reflection” on his role and his future, on whether he truly has the energy in him for one last fight.

“It’s a matter of whether I can help the team, and I’ll have a look at that this week,” he said. “Every time things don’t go so well, age plays a part, and you know what, they may be right. I’m 110 in two years’ time. That may be time to wrap it up. But I’ll see how it goes.

View image in fullscreen Tempers flare between Rangers manager Derek McInnes (right) and his opposite number, Martin O’Neill, at Celtic Park. Photograph: Andrew Milligan/PA

“Let me generalise a little bit. I got an opportunity to come back last October which I never thought would happen in my life. Winning the league, the game against Hearts, was one of the great moments of my managerial time. But even then, I was still thinking about whether you can still have the energy, the desire. There’s nothing great about getting old, I’ll tell you that.”

What is true of O’Neill may also be true of a few of his players. Is Callum McGregor, club legend but now 33 years of age and increasingly off the pace, still fit for purpose? Does Liam Scales need replacing? Does Kieran Tierney still have the legs? What exactly is James Forrest still doing about the place? And in the meantime, would you remotely trust the Celtic board – still essentially hollow of footballing expertise – to oversee the required transition?

Not on this evidence. The summer signings – Kasper Høgh, Mika Baur, Camilo Durán – largely disappeared from view.

Quick Guide Roundup: Vrancken bewildered by VAR as Hearts frustrated at Kilmarnock Show Wouter Vrancken was left bewildered by the “strange” video assistant referee decision to rule out an early Hearts goal in their 1-1 draw at bottom-placed Kilmarnock. The Jambos thought they had gone ahead in the 11th minute when Laurent Mendy’s effort – which appeared to be going wide – was diverted into the net by the Killie defender Cathal McCarthy. But the VAR, Matthew MacDermid, advised Duncan Nicolson to rule it out as the ball had accidentally struck Mendy’s hand. Killie went ahead a few minutes later through a Jamie McCart own goal before Stephen Kingsley equalised in the 86th minute (pictured). But Vrancken cited similarities with the recent incident involving Manchester United’s Harry Maguire against Ipswich and felt Mendy’s inadvertent handball should have been rendered irrelevant by McCarthy heading the ball into the net. “For me, when it’s such a clear situation, it’s strange that the VAR comes in between and rules wrong,” said the Belgian. “We had a meeting last week about the laws of the game and the refs did their explanation but when you don’t see them applied in the game, then I’m thinking this is strange." Martin Boyle ended Hibernian’s losing streak at home after they fought back to claim a point in a 1-1 draw against Aberdeen. The Dons went ahead in the 17th minute with a composed finish from former Hibs striker Kevin Nisbet. Managerless Hibs – with John Potter in interim charge after David Gray’s midweek sacking – looked bereft of confidence for long spells. However, the Leith side – who had lost six successive games at Easter Road – earned a share of the spoils when Boyle levelled from the penalty spot in the 62nd minute after Jack Milne dragged Jason Kerr to the ground. Steven Pressley praised Joe Westley for the bravery he showed by playing in Dundee's 2-1 home win over Motherwell. The former Burnley striker fractured his cheekbone against Hearts a fortnight ago but declared himself available after deciding against having surgery. Instead, he played wearing a protective mask and nett Dundee’s opening goal from the penalty spot before Bradley Fink doubled their advantage. Alex Lowry pulled one back for the visitors just before the break but the home side held on. Pressley said: “Joe showed great courage. But he gave a wonderful performance, without any trepidation. Joe was fearless in everything he did and to score a goal is really important for him because he lives off them." Jim Goodwin hailed his side’s performance as the perfect tonic as Dundee United defeated St Mirren 3-0 in a one-sided contest in Paisley, with first-half goals from Jesse Randall, Lyall Cameron and Kevin Ciubotaru. It was Goodwin’s first appearance in the dugout since a recent health scare and the United manager said: “On a personal note, it was great to be back. Certainly the best medicine that I could have hoped for was that type of result and performance." A stunning set-piece strike from Enes Alic in the sixth minute of stoppage time secured a dramatic 1-1 draw for 10-man St Johnstone against Falkirk. Falkirk took advantage of Cheick Diabaté’s 54th-minute red card to seize the lead through Ethan Ross on the hour. But Alic found the top corner from 25 yards to move Simo Valakari’s side up to sixth place. Press Association Photograph: Mark Runnacles/Shutterstock Editorial Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

There was fury here but precious little focus, plenty of passion but no real patterns of play, no order to the chaos, no real idea of how to keep the ball or fashion a chance. Rangers dominated the central areas, where Dan Neil and Nicolas Raskin are already forging a formidable partnership and James Penrice merrily stomped all over the place.

O’Neill gambled on a back five, on Luke McCowan in a sort of withdrawn winger role, discarded both at half-time, rolled through his substitutions, but the plan never really emerged from the fog. Celtic are basically like the tangled ball of printer cables and headphone wires in the bottom drawer, where you’re never quite sure whether you’re unpicking the knots or making them tighter.

Naderi’s goal, bundled in from close range after Kim Min-su’s long-range effort was parried helpfully into his path by Viljami Sinisalo, was simply the most consequential emblem of Rangers’ superiority here. Emmanuel Fernandez got a rough ride early on, Tierney clipped the bar from distance and Ivor Pandur made a fine save from Colby Donovan early in the second half. That was basically it, as far as explicit threat went. Donovan’s header was the only Celtic shot on target.

“For a young team, it’s brilliant that they can take the good from this,” said McInnes. “Coming to places like this, it won’t get much more difficult. It’s only three points, but in the context of the season it was important for lots of reasons.” He knows, of course, that Rangers are not the finished article. But right now there is a power vacuum at the top of Scottish football and his improving side may as well be the one to fill it.

Sports.title: Jonathan David earns Atlético precious win over 10-man Real Madrid in fractious derby
Sports.content:
Diego Simeone said it had been a special week in Madrid, a “tremendous energy about the city”, and it closed the way he wanted. He had enjoyed the Formula One, he said, and he had enjoyed going to see Shakira. He enjoyed this even more, at least he did by the time the last of many, many blows on the referee’s whistle brought it to an end, sending him sprinting up the tunnel punching the air. Two-nil up against 10 men through goals from Álex Grimaldo and Jonathan David, seemingly in control, a late strike from Antonio Rüdiger awoke old ghosts and brought tension to the final minutes, but they had done it.

“A lot has happened in Madrid this week but this was the only thing that mattered in his mind and mine,” Atlético’s goalkeeper, Jan Oblak, said. José Mourinho’s first derby back ended in defeat and recriminations: he turned up at the press conference with a picture of two moments in which he felt that Atlético players – Lee Kang-in and Cristian Romero – should have been sent off, and insisting that the story of the derby was there. And yet there are other questions: over the way Dean Huijsen gave away the penalty and got the red card that tilted the game against them, and the way Real played. How little they did until that moment when, briefly, they appeared to have a lifeline.

A familiar foe had defeated him. It is 13 years since these managers met in this fixture, their last time the day that Atlético finally broke a curse and won the Copa del Rey at the Santiago Bernabéu. That night, Mourinho was sent off and didn’t go to get his runner’s-up medal from the king as Atlético won their first derby in 13 years. His return to Real Madrid has been driven in part by nostalgia and it was like old times in the press room. At times in the first half here it was like old times too. Which were not always good. Mourinho and Simeone are “companions of war”, the Real manager had said, and so it was.

Twenty minutes passed before the first shot, Aurélien Tchouaméni striking over from 25 yards, and it wasn’t until the 39th that there was one on target. That came, perhaps inevitably, from outside the area and Oblak pushed Arda Guler’s effort away. Otherwise, not a huge amount else was happening. Not when it came to actual football, anyway: it had been heating up almost from the beginning, Guler the first to confront the referee after he was fouled by Álex Baena. To which he would respond by fouling Baena back.

From the bench, something was said and Simeone was booked; the scene was set. This was a battle played out down there as much as out on the pitch, where it was tough and tight. When Lee went looking for David with a cross towards the back post after quarter of an hour, it was the closest anyone had got, physically, to either goal, and immediately Real broke up the right. The roar that greeted Marc Pubill’s tackle to take out Kylian Mbappé said something about the fear it was in transition that Atlético would be caught. The fear or, from Mourinho’s point of view, the hope. The plan, in fact, and they would wait for the moment.

The hosts had more of the ball and the territory but they tended to approach with caution. The lines of white shirts before them didn’t offer them the space to run into, so they were inclined to go to wide, which almost always meant the right wing. Another advance on that side led to a moment soon after when Ibrahima Konaté’s moment of doubt saw David take the ball from him inside the area, leading to Giuliano Simeone flashing wide. Then Thibaut Courtois had to dive to push a Lee cross away. At the other end Vinícius Júnior shot over twice – both over, both from distance – before the half’s most significant moment. Which, appropriately, wasn’t about the play.

Instead, Jude Bellingham slid in to tackle Romero and the referee showed him a red. Bellingham was incensed, his teammates and Real Madrid’s bench were too, and the video assistant referee was engaged. The referee, Miguel Ángel Ortiz, who was struggling to control this, was called to the screen to watch it again. There, he saw Romero’s studs hit Bellingham’s knee. The decision was rescinded, the Englishman’s card taken away. Atlético felt it should have been red. When Lee’s studs went in on Federico Valverde, Real did too.

Confrontations continued, angry words were exchanged, but as they went off at half-time, chances didn’t come with them. Two red cards did now: at half-time Atlético’s goalkeeper coach and Real’s assistant were sent off.

The second half began with Koke introduced and Baena immediately forcing a save. It was Atlético’s first shot on target, and it was the start of an entirely different game. Their second shot soon after would give them the lead, and an advantage that was even bigger than that. A long ball over the top from David Hancko dropped out of the sky and into the run of Simeone and, as he tried to bring it down and head into the area, Dean Huijsen dragged him down. Ortiz pointed to the spot; he was also called to the VAR screen again. Not to overturn the penalty, that could not have been clearer, but to change the colour of the card. Huijsen walked, Grimaldo scored and the Metropolitano exploded.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

View image in fullscreen Real Madrid's Dean Huijsen fouls Giuliano Simeone leading to a penalty and a red card for the defender. Photograph: Juan Carlos Lucas/Zuma Press Wire/Shutterstock

You suspected that Mourinho would too. First, he removed Guler and Vinícius to introduce Yan Diomandé and Rüdiger. Vinícius had done little, racking up just 22 touches, and a readjustment was required but there have been times when decisions like that – the Brazilian’s removal late in last year’s clásico, on a night that Real Madrid actually won, was the beginning of the end for Xabi Alonso – have caused splits. What this does is yet to be seen. The change didn’t have any real impact, either. Instead, Atlético doubled the lead. Again, it came from the right where Lee, who was outstanding, worked it to Simeone. His low cross, bent behind Madrid’s back four, was perfect. Six yards out, David turned it in.

David was withdrawn immediately, Julián Alvarez replacing him to whistles from the home fans. Still Atlético came, and the Argentinian so nearly had the third when Courtois made an extraordinary save from Romero and as the ball dropped Konaté rescued Madrid twice, the second time clearing off the line from Alvarez. Simeone smelt blood – Ademola Lookman was introduced too. Real Madrid, it seemed, could do nothing. Oblak barely saw them. Not once in that second half did Real touch the ball in his area, until they scored in the 89th minute. Kylian Mbappé barely touched the ball anywhere. Inside Atlético’s half, a pigeon sat pecking at the grass for a good few minutes, uninterrupted by even the briefest of counterattacks.

When Diomandé at last got away with 15 minutes to go, Oblak saved a shot that was hit straight at him, the opportunity to maybe make a match of the final minutes wasted. Or so it seemed. From a dead ball, Rüdiger headed in to give them a hope, a few minutes of a rebellion that was brief and incomplete, unlike Simeone’s week.

Sports.title: ‘Mixed emotions’ for Farke as Leeds stay unbeaten with Crystal Palace stalemate
Sports.content:
Perhaps it is testament to the progress Leeds have made since returning to the Premier League just over a year ago that there was frustration at failing to move up to third after drawing with Crystal Palace. Instead, Daniel Farke’s team enter the prolonged international break in fifth and unbeaten, which is a fine achievement in itself.

Apart from Tyrick Mitchell’s disallowed goal, neither side gave much impression they would secure the points. For Palace, it was a first clean sheet of the season, having conceded at least twice in their opening four games, relieving pressure on Pierre Sage, while the hosts endured their first blank.

A victory by two clear goals would have meant a best-ever start to a Premier League campaign for Leeds but they were blunt in the final third. There was even a level of discontent amid a ponderous performance with fans chanting “forward” as they failed to replicate the thrashing of Newcastle on Monday.

“Mixed emotions,” Farke said. “We would have preferred to win, but the reality is it is 38 game days. It is not always magic nights under the floodlights, champagne football, you overrun the opponent and score goals for fun. Sometimes it is a scruffy Sunday afternoon when you have to dig in. This was one of these games.”

Farke is into the final year of his contract and signing a new deal is a priority for him and the club. His stature has grown over the past 10 months, with Leeds the fifth-best performing team in the division since December 2025 and the German will likely be rewarded in the coming weeks for bringing stability to the club as Leeds aim to build on strong foundations.

The most notable moment of the opening quarter here came when Walter Benítez took too long to distribute the ball. The referee, Adam Herczeg – making his Premier League debut and fully aware of the rules – awarded Leeds a corner as punishment. It was a tentative game in the autumn sunshine, lacking intensity and quality, with Ao Tanaka snatching at a shot the closest anyone got to threatening a goal.

Around the half-hour something akin to a football match broke out as nervousness was replaced by urgency. Jørgen Strand Larsen and Quinten Timber engineered a chance for Palace which was blocked and allowed Leeds to break through Noah Okafor down the left, although his cross was turned behind.

Palace had the greater quality, with Adam Wharton and Timber comfortable in possession in the middle of the park, while Yéremy Pino whizzed around in the hope of finding an opener. It was controlled play, as the visitors took their time in the buildup, although there was often very little at the end of it as James Trafford was left unthreatened.

View image in fullscreen James Justin stretches to block an effort from Eddie Nketiah. Photograph: Greig Cowie/Shutterstock

Leeds on the other hand would burst into life for brief moments as the full-backs flew forward, changing the dynamic in an instant but Palace’s centre-backs and wing-backs were built to deal with these rapid transitions, leaving Dominic Calvert-Lewin starved of service. Benítez could relax and re-read the laws of the game, having failed to face a single shot on target in the opening 40 minutes.

Palace pushed the fast-forward button at the break and Mitchell put the ball in the back of the net from a fine move down the right. The glory turned to anguish when the video assistant referee intervened to show Anan Khalaili was offside in the buildup, causing an eruption inside Elland Road.

Leeds were sluggish but the warning from Mitchell caused a reaction and they were almost ahead when Calvert-Lewin’s only real chance was saved by Benítez. The England striker was given too much space to get on the end of a cross but his sidefooted volley was weak.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

There was a touch of menace in the game as Tanaka and Wharton were booked in quick succession, the first for a cynical foul and the latter after lunging in late without a hope of winning the ball, ensuring Herczeg was far busier than the two goalkeepers.

Leeds were completely ineffective in open play, Ethan Ampadu engaged in a long-throwathon. Every few minutes he would trot to a sidelineto pick up the ball and hurl it into the box but Palace were alive to the danger. “We had many set pieces today, but also today we didn’t have the best quality of the delivery,” Farke said.

Palace edged the match and Daichi Kamada could have won it late on but his header drifted inches wide. Sage will be relieved to see his defence so well organised and untroubled after conceding 11 in the first four games, leading to plenty of early scrutiny on his appointment. “Especially when I read the social media, there’s a big pressure.” Sage said.

“But you know, I don’t care about that. I do my job with honesty, I give my best with my skills and my limits. And in the end, I have no regrets with what I do.”

Sports.title: Andros Townsend avoids injury after bizarre pitch roller incident in Thailand
Sports.content:
The former England winger Andros Townsend has joked Stoke away “wasn’t so bad after all” following a bizarre incident in Thailand where he was run over by a pitch roller.

The former Tottenham and Crystal Palace attacker currently plays in Thai League 1 for PT Prachuap and made headlines on Saturday night when a clip emerged on social media which showed the 35-year-old being taken out before a fixture at Pattani.

Townsend was warming up when a member of staff at Pattani appeared to lose control of the pitch roller and it crashed into the 13-cap England international. The left leg of the Prachuap player briefly got stuck under the vehicle, but he did feature off the bench late on in the 3-0 win.

Regular ITV pundit Townsend later took to Instagram to make light of the incident, referencing one of his recent posts in which he contrasted a sun-drenched Thai away trip with previous visits to Stoke’s windswept stadium.

Townsend said on his Instagram story: “It turns out Stoke away wasn’t so bad after all. Swipe to see why.”

Another post described Townsend as ‘The King of Memes in Thai League history’ and he replied “trust me” with four laughing emojis.

Sports.title: Holmberg rescues point for Arsenal but Manchester United off the mark in WSL
Sports.content:
Arsenal were mightily relieved as a 95th-minute Smilla Holmberg volley rescued a point at home to a much-improved Manchester United side, but the draw will not be enough to eradicate concerns about how far behind the leaders Manchester City Renée Slegers’ team are slipping already and how frequently they seem to struggle to break down a low block.

A defiant Manchester United stunned the north Londoners as Eva Olid’s side claimed the first point of her tenure with a performance that defied all of the pre-match scripts, but it was very nearly a victory, had it not been for Holmberg’s last-gasp back-post finish from Leah Williamson’s deep, diagonal ball into the box, which finally broke the visitors’ stubborn resistance.

Widely criticised for their dismal displays in their opening two defeats against London City Lionesses and Chelsea, Manchester United were heavily tipped to struggle again at the Emirates but an encouraging defensive effort and an against-the-run-of-play Julia Zigiotti Olme strike gave them a precious lead in a display that will buy the former Hearts manager Olid plenty of time to continue working on her style on the training ground and quieten those doubting her.

Instead it will be Arsenal now facing scrutiny as they failed to win at home for a second straight game and slipped four points behind the defending champions, Manchester City, after just three rounds of fixtures. Last term, Manchester City dropped points in only four games and the early-season leaders have a 100% record so far. Arsenal’s next two WSL games are away to Chelsea and Manchester City.

Quick Guide Spurs put seven past Crystal Palace Show Olivia Holdt struck a second-half hat-trick as Tottenham continued their promising start to the new Women’s Super League season by thrashing 10-player Crystal Palace 7-0 at Selhurst Park. The Eagles had midfielder Fuka Tsunoda sent off after only eight minutes for a late foul on Cathinka Tandberg. Spurs – who drew at Liverpool last week after opening with a win over West Ham – had twice struck the woodwork in the first half before Denmark forward Holdt’s treble took the game away from the home side. Summer signing Victoria Pelova, substitute Shekiera Martinez and Amanda Nilden all scored in the closing stages. Netherlands midfielder Pelova then slotted in a seventh during added time to leave Martin Ho’s side second in the table. Everton snatched a 1-0 win at West Ham after a stoppage-time own goal from Irons defender Laia Codina. Both sides looked set for a point before Codina nodded into her own net from a free-kick by Yuka Momiki as the Toffees moved up to fifth. Lynn Wilms scored an 89th-minute equaliser as Aston Villa snatched a 1-1 draw against Brighton, who had gone ahead in the first half through Gabby George, leaving each club still in search of a first WSL win. Press Association Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

“It’s not ideal, it’s not what we wanted at all, four lost points,” Slegers admitted, reflected on consecutive home draws, but she added: “It’s round three in the WSL, there are a lot of games left to play. Let’s see in May, how it ends. Not converting dominance into wins, that’s something we have to look at. We believe in the quality of the squad. When that starts clicking, it’s going to be really good.”

In truth, this was a result that Arsenal could ill-afford, especially after last weekend’s goalless draw at home to the newly promoted side Crystal Palace, where the north Londoners were surprisingly wasteful in the final third. Slegers’ team had scored just one goal from 43 shots across their opening two league fixtures. Surely, therefore, a home match against a side who conceded five goals last time out was the perfect opportunity to banish any concerns of a lack of clinical quality in the final third? Think again.

View image in fullscreen Manchester United’s Julia Zigiotti Olme celebrates scoring against Arsenal. Photograph: Paul Harding/WSL/WSL Football/Getty Images

The hosts did create good openings and looked to have control of the midfield. Their winger Lisa Baum shot straight at Phallon Tullis-Joyce early on and was providing dangerous crosses from the left. Mariona Caldentey also went close, curling just wide and Tullis-Joyce made a fine save to keep out Stina Blackstenius’ header. Nevertheless, it had been United’s Elisabeth Terland who went closest in the first half, being thwarted by two excellent Misa Rodríguez saves in quick succession.

Arsenal stepped up the pressure after half-time but Georgia Stanway – one of Arsenal’s better performers for the rest of the game – made a costly error as she tried to play a simple pass back towards the centre-back Steph Catley that carelessly rolled the ball into the path of Zigiotti Olme instead. The grateful Manchester United midfielder confidently stepped the ball around Catley and slotted through the legs of Rodríguez. The Emirates was astonished. The United bench, jubilant.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to Moving the Goalposts No topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

View image in fullscreen Phallon Tullis-Joyce leaping up to make a crucial save to keep Arsenal at bay. Photograph: Nina Farooqi/ZUMA Press Wire/Shutterstock

From then on, it was ‘backs to the wall’ for the visitors, much like it was during the majority of this fixture last term, which ended goalless. Tullis-Joyce dived low and strong to keep out a Cailtin Foord effort and United battled well to clear the danger from several set pieces as the home side grew increasingly frustrated. The crowd eventually erupted as the substitute Holmberg earned them a point and Manchester United’s players fell to their knees.

Quick Guide WSL Saturday roundup: Chelsea's Potter and Malard sink Birmingham Show Chelsea and London City Lionesses climbed the Women’s Super League table with respective victories over Birmingham and Charlton. After thumping Manchester United 5-0 last weekend, Chelsea won again as Lexi Potter and Melvine Malard secured a 2-0 win. Potter found the roof of the net in the eighth minute (the celebrations pictured above) and in the 71st minute the France star Malard made a quick impact from the bench with her first goal at Stamford Bridge. Chelsea moved up to second and with their goal difference were likely to stay there. London City lost 2-1 to West Ham last time out but impressed in a 4-1 triumph at promoted Charlton. Isobel Goodwin’s double had London City two goals ahead after 15 minutes and, despite Jodie Hutton halving the deficit in the 39th minute with a fine finish, Jana Fernández restored their advantage before half-time. The German forward Nicole Anyomi made sure the outcome was no longer in doubt with the Lionesses’ fourth after 76 minutes. They sit third, a point behind Chelsea. Press Association Photograph: Yaroslav Dunka/Shutterstock Editorial Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

Olid was pleased with their display, though, explaining: “After losing 5-0, the focus this week was the defensive shape, because I think the attack will come. Implementing a new style of play needs time. But the effort, the hard work, the intensity, that can never be missing. It was so important to see that today. That is the minimum. Now, from here, little-by-little, we will improve the attacking style.”

Sports.title: Why Sunderland did not get penalty after Elliot Anderson handball in incident you may have missed
Sports.content:
Why Sunderland did not get penalty after Elliot Anderson handball in incident you may have missed

Sunderland were controversially denied a penalty during their defeat to Manchester City on Sunday.

The Black Cats' 5-3 defeat at the Etihad Stadium could have been different had Elliot Anderson been penalised for a handball inside the City penalty area.

2 Sunderland were denied a penalty for handball during their loss to City Credit: Getty

The midfielder appeared to swat the ball away with his hand whilst jostling for possession with Enzo Le Fee.

Anderson then hooked the ball clear as the Sunderland man appealed for a spot-kick.

Sunderland denied a penalty

His calls for a penalty fell on deaf ears, though, with referee Robert Jones opting not to award a spot-kick.

VAR also decided against intervening to overturn the on-field decision.

talkSPORT understands the officials deemed Anderson's handball as accidental. As a result, he was not penalised despite the ball hitting his hand.

That's not how Sunderland boss Regis Le Bris saw it, saying post-match: "It was hard to see that as not a handball.

"It is what it is and we have to accept the decision. It's hard to comment."

Busy afternoon for VAR

It was not the only contentious decision VAR had to deal with during the match.

Erling Haaland's late strike was initially ruled out for offside by the assistant referee.

However, a VAR review determined Josko Gvardiol had been onside during the build-up, with the goal awarded.

Explaining the decision on X, the Premier League Match Centre said: "VAR checked the referee's call of no goal for offside and determined that Gvardiol was in an offside position in the build-up and recommended that the goal was awarded."

Haaland's effort nine minutes from time completed the scoring on a frantic afternoon in Manchester.

City had twice been pegged back by Brian Brobbey during the first half after Enzo Fernandez and Rayan Cherki put them ahead.

A brace from Antoine Semenyo either side of half-time established a two-goal advantage, though.

Brobbey completed his hat-trick just two minutes later to reapply the pressure to Enzo Maresca's side.

Haaland's fifth Premier League goal of the season was ultimately enough to clinch all three points for his side and maintain their 100 per cent record.

Sports.title: Michael Carrick told he’ll be sacked by January as Gary Neville slams ‘worst ever’ Manchester United
Sports.content:
Michael Carrick's days as Manchester United manager are numbered, talkSPORT's Perry Groves said following a 1-1 draw with Fulham.

Matheus Cunha's deflected strike in the 89th minute ensured the Red Devils left Craven Cottage with a point after Lisandro Martinez's comical own goal put the hosts in front.



4 Cunha's first league goal this season spared United's blushes Credit: Getty

The result means United have won just once from their opening five league matches and, perhaps more worryingly, are still yet to keep a clean sheet.

Groves, who was at Craven Cottage on commentary for talkSPORT, was especially critical of United's urgency, or lack of, throughout the contest.

"I'm looking at this and I said Man United are a half-and-half team," Groves said.



"When they close down, they do it half-heartedly. When they drop deep, they don't close the ball down when it's in their own final third.

"I can't see Michael Carrick lasting half the season."

What did Perry Groves say about Manchester United's display against Fulham?

Groves added that the draw, which helped United to their fifth point of the season, was 'papering over the cracks'.



"They had a bit of urgency when they were 1-0 down, but it's a different scenario," Groves continued.

"When you're one or 2-0 down, it's easier because the opposition sits deeper, so you then think you'll take chances.



"They should be doing that before they go 1-0 down in the 63rd minute."

Fulham could, and perhaps should, have been ahead by more when Martinez inadvertently poked the ball into his own net after Senne Lammens parried Calvin Bassey's effort.

4 Carrick was handed a permanent deal before the end of last season Credit: Getty

Unfortunately for the Cottagers, summer signing Gonzalo Garcia seemed to have left his scoring boots elsewhere as he spurned a number of good chances.



But the fact Garcia enjoyed a number of promising opportunities against United had Groves believing rival players now circle matches against the Red Devils in their calendar, such is the number of high-quality chances they tend to give up.

Manchester United 'got away with it' against Fulham

"From a player's point of view, I think they're nice to play against," Groves said.

"I don't think they really test you. We've seen it in the first half where Fulham played through them fairly easily. There was a period of 20 minutes in that first half where every time Fulham went forward, they looked like they were going to score.

"If Gonzalo Garcia had his boots on the right feet in the first half, this could have been a lot worse.



"I just think Manchester United have got away with it."

4 The Red Devils haven't convinced in their opening five fixtures Credit: Getty

Neville: 'The worst 15 minutes from Man United ever'

Man United's performance in the first part of the second half had club legend Gary Neville seething as he was left astounded by the team's lack of work-ethic.

Neville said on commentary for Sky Sports: "I’ve watched Man United since the age of 5 and that’s the worst 15 minutes I’ve ever seen them pla."

Neville added after the game: "Both teams were the same. I called them mannequins. They were mannequins. I've never seen a United team walk around as much as that. No alertness, no aliveness. No 'on your toes'. You should always be on your toes.



"Always shifting up two or three yards. They were just walking when Fulham were in possession. Fulham had 46 passes in the first couple of minutes to get their first shot.

"46 chances - Fulham against Man Utd. I don't know how many over-ten-pass sequences Fulham had in that game, but the international break has come at a great time. There needs to be a rebalance."

Neville continued: "I've never seen a Man Utd team walk out of possession as much as that. Michael has just said there was nothing wrong with the team's energy.

4 Man United's application at Craven Cottage was a red flag for Neville Credit: Getty



"Michael has got to stop defending them. I get why he's defending them; he's loyal, he wants his players to work for him, and obviously there's a long way to go in the season."

For Carrick, the international break may have arrived at an opportune time given the stark contrast in results from when he first took over to now.

The brutal stats exposing Manchester United's downturn under Michael Carrick

In Carrick's 17 league games at the helm last term, United averaged 2.3 points per game.

But that figure has dropped to just one point per game this season, hinting that something is not going according to plan within his set-up.



In another alarming stat, the five points accrued by United under Carrick this term is their joint-fewest from the first five games of a Premier League season.

According to talkSPORT's chief football correspondent Alex Crook, United's bleak start is perhaps emblematic of their malaise in recent years.

"There's just an acceptance of these low standards at Manchester United, that dropping two points away from home at Fulham isn't a disaster that it maybe once was," Crook said on commentary.

"I think what Michael Carrick has got to do, and he did it in the second half of last season, is change the whole mindset in that dressing room."



Carrick now has multiple weeks to re-wire the mentality of his players before they return to action on October 10 at home against Tottenham Hotspur, who sit bottom of the table.

Sports.title: EFL club buy one million bricks salvaged from hospital for new stadium
Sports.content:
EFL club buy one million bricks salvaged from hospital for new stadium

Birmingham City have taken another step towards the completion of their new 62,000-capacity stadium.

The Championship club have purchased one million bricks from the former City Hospital to help with construction of the ground.

3 Birmingham have purchased one million bricks from City Hospital for their new stadium Credit: PA

It comes as they plan to leave St. Andrew's by 2030 as part of a £2billion regeneration project.

The redevelopment in the Bordesley Green area of Birmingham will see the introduction of a new Sports Quarter.

Backed by their owners Knighthead, Blues will leave their home of 120 years, which currently holds 29,400 fans.

Birmingham stadium latest

Ahead of the move, bricks have been bought from the city's historic former hospital.

City Hospital closed in 2024 after more than 130 years in operation, having been founded in 1887.

The bricks have been cleaned by specialists ahead of being used for the new development.

It is understood the hospital bricks will form part of the 12 brick chimney-style towers at the new stadium.

Images of the planned venue show the towers on display in a nod to the brickwork which used to sit on the site.

A record of how the bricks were manufactured, stored and transported will also be displayed once the stadium is completed.

The club previously revealed their aim to have moved into their new home by the start of the 2029/30 season.

3 The hospital bricks will form part of the 12 chimney-style towers in the stadium design Credit: Collect

However, their flexible completion goal is currently during 2030 for the ground, which was unveiled in November last year.

Previous stadium plans

Birmingham previously unveiled plans for a new stadium during their time in the Premier League.

In 2004, Blues announced a proposed 55,000-capacity stadium to replace St. Andrew's.

Those plans would have also seen the introduction of a sports village in the city.

However, the proposals were ultimately shelved, with the club remaining at their existing ground.

Birmingham have played home matches at St. Andrew's since it was opened in 1906.

3 Birmingham plan to move into their new 62,000-stadium by 2030 Credit: BIRMINGHAM CITY FC

The ground was most recently renovated between 2020 and 2023, with the rebuilding of the lower tiers in the Kop and Tilton Road Stands.

This season marks the club's second campaign back in the Championship.

Birmingham secured an immediate return to the second tier in 2025 following their relegation to League One.

Chris Davies' side currently sit tenth after eight matches following a 2-2 draw at home against Middlesbrough on Saturday.

Sports.title: Ronald Koeman Jr breaks down in tears on pitch during emotional tribute to his mum
Sports.content:
Ronald Koeman Jr breaks down in tears on pitch during emotional tribute to his mum

Ronald Koeman Jr was visibly emotional during a tribute to his late mother during Telstar's match against AZ Alkmaar.

The Eredivisie clash was paused in the 13th minute for an applause in honour of Bartina Koeman.



2 Koeman Jr broke down in tears during a tribute to his late mother Credit: ESPN

Her passing aged 65 was announced on Wednesday following a battle with breast cancer.

Bartina was the wife of former Netherlands captain and manager Ronald Koeman.

Tribute to Bartina Koeman

She was also Koeman Jr's mother, with the goalkeeper on the pitch for Telstar at the time of the tribute.



He could be seen wiping away tears as her picture was displayed on the big screen inside AZ's AFAS Stadion.

Supporters from both clubs paid tribute during the minute's applause.

Meanwhile, Telstar fans held sparklers aloft as they honoured Bartina's life.



Koeman Jr had joined on with the applause before using his shirt to wipe his eyes as he broke down in tears.

As the minute's applause concluded, he clapped the crowd to thank them for their tributes.



AZ went on to win the match 1-0 thanks to Mexx Meerdink's first half goal.

The result leaves Telstar 13th in the Eredivisie standings after seven matches this season.

However, they are now winless in their last six despite Koeman Jr scoring twice against Cambuur earlier this month, becoming the first goalkeeper in Eredivisie history to score two goals in one match.

The 31-year-old was making his first appearance since his mother's death was announced.



Bartina had been married to Koeman for 41 years prior to her passing, with the couple having three children together.

The former Everton manager stepped down as national team boss following their World Cup exit in order to care for her.

Announcing the tragic news on social media, Koeman wrote: "With deep sorrow, but also with great pride and love, we say goodbye to my wonderful wife, our dearest mom and grandma.”

The news also came after Koeman Jr had welcomed the birth of his first child earlier this month.



2 A minute's applause was held in honour of Bartina during AZ's win over Telstar Credit: ESPN

Bartina was first diagnosed with breast cancer back in 2010, from which she recovered after receiving treatment.

Having recovered, the disease returned in 2018 before she was diagnosed with chronic breast cancer two years ago.

Koeman announced last year, though, that the cancer cells had spread.

Sports.title: Real Madrid insist ‘dreadful’ referee missed two Atletico Madrid red cards in furious statement after derby defeat
Sports.content:
Real Madrid insist both Cristian Romero and Kang-In Lee wrongly avoided red cards during derby defeat to Atletico Madrid.

After a 2-1 defeat at the Wanda Metropolitano on Sunday, Los Blancos put out a furious statement blasting the performance of referee Miguel Angel Ortiz Arias, claiming his perceived incompetence turned the match in favour of Atleti.

4 There's sour grapes from Real Madrid after the derby Credit: Getty

The first incident they're raging about saw Atletico Madrid defender Romero caught Jude Bellingham on the knee as the Real Madrid midfielder sild in to try and tackle him.

Bellingham was initially booked before referee Miguel Angel Ortiz Arias was sent to the pitchside monitor to review the incident.

Romero was then booked instead – but he might have been lucky not to receive stronger punishment.

Bellingham was visibly in pain after taking studs to his knee, but the England star was able to play on.

Meanwhile, Federico Valverde was left in a heap after his ankle was trodden on by Atletico player Lee. Lee did not receive a yellow or red card.

Real Madrid rage at referee

The Real Madrid players let their feelings known at the official during and after the match with a video of Bellingham emerging post-match of him taking umbrage at Atletico not receiving two reds.

Manager Jose Mourinho brandished a picture of the point of contact between Lee's foot and Valverde's ankle during his press conference as he lamented the referee's performance.

But the ill-feeling didn't stop there with the club later putting out a statement slamming Ortiz.

In a statement titled 'A dreadful refereeing performance decides the derby', Real Madrid said: "Real Madrid lost at the Metropolitano in a derby marked by the poor officiating of Ortiz Arias, who failed to send off Cuti Romero in the first half for stepping on Bellingham's knee (despite reviewing the play on the monitor) and Kang-In Lee for stepping on Valverde's left ankle.

"Both decisions shaped the match, which was decided in the second half in favour of Atletico.

"Until the 30th minute, the game had very few dangerous plays. But from that point on, controversy took over the derby.

"In the 35th minute, during a contested ball, Bellingham got to the ball before Cuti Romero, and the Atletico defender planted his studs into the left knee of the Madrid player.

"Ortiz Arias initially booked our player but was called by Trujillo Suárez to review the incident on the monitor.

"After watching the replay, he rescinded the card from Bellingham and issued a yellow card to the Atletico defender instead of sending him off.

"Nine minutes later, the referee made another crucial error by not penalizing Kang-In Lee for a challenge on Valverde, where he struck him with his studs on the left ankle.

"Ortiz Arias was close to the incident but did not show a red card (or even a yellow card) to the Atletico player, nor was he alerted by Trujillo Suarez on this occasion."

4 Mourinho's actions in his press conference were rather tame compared to the statement from the club that followed Credit: Getty

Atletico Madrid 2-1 Real Madrid

The first meeting of these two rivals saw three yellow cards in the first half alone, with Romero's centre-back teammate Marc Pubill also going into the book – along with Atletico boss Diego Simeone, just six minutes into the contest at the Estadio Metropolitano.

Real Madrid were then reduced to ten men at the start of the second half when defender Dean Huijsen was sent off with Atleti taking the lead moments later through an Alejandro Grimaldo penalty.

A matter of minutes into the second half, Dean Huijsen saw red for a foul in the box, for which Atleti were awarded a penalty.

Alex Grimaldo duly dispatched from 12 yards to break the deadlock.

And it soon got even better for the hosts, who doubled their lead through Jonathan David.

Antonio Rudiger pulled one back for Los Blancos but they couldn't find an equaliser as Atleti claimed the bragging rights with a 2-1 win.

4 Huijsen was sent off with more than half an hour left to play Credit: Getty

4 Atleti moved a point ahead of Real Madrid with the win Credit: Getty

Atleti fared well in recent home LaLiga clashes with their bitter rivals, winning two and drawing one of the previous three prior to Sunday's game.

Simeone's side came into this game off the back of two comprehensive league victories, keeping clean sheets in both.

Real Madrid, with Jose Mourinho back for a second spell in charge, had been in similarly good nick, winning their previous three matches in all competitions.

But now they're fourth in the Spanish top flight and six points off early season pace setters Barcelona.

Sports.title: Derek McInnes achieves rare Old Firm history only matched by one Rangers manager
Sports.content:
Derek McInnes achieves rare Old Firm history only matched by one Rangers manager

Derek McInnes made history as he led Rangers to victory over Celtic in the Scottish Premiership.

Rangers' 1-0 win at Celtic Park was their second triumph over their Old Firm rivals in the space of eight days, having run out 3-0 winners at Ibrox in the League Cup last Sunday.

2 McInnes has a 100 per cent record in Old Firm games as Rangers boss so far Credit: Getty

Naderi helps McInnes make history

Ryan Naderi's first-half strike proved decisive and saw Rangers close the gap to Celtic at the top of the Premiership table to two points ahead of the first international break of the season.

And McInnes has now done something only one previous Rangers manager had ever managed.

The 55-year-old, who won the Scottish Premiership title and Scottish Cup with Rangers as a player, became the club's second boss to win both of their first Old Firm derbies in charge in all competitions.

Graeme Souness was the first to achieve that feat back in 1986, during his time as player-manager.

McInnes took over at Rangers this summer after coming agonisingly close to ending the Old Firm's 41-year grip on the Scottish title with Hearts last season.

And after a rocky start which saw them dumped out of Europa League qualifying by Poland's Jagiellonia Bialystok then suffer the same fate against Czech side Jablonec in the Conference League, McInnes has overseen six straight domestic wins – with Rangers keeping five clean sheets in the process.

Rangers are chasing their first league title since the 2020/21 campaign.

They've seen Celtic win the last five on the trot, moving to a record 56 overall last term.

McInnes reflects on 'worthy win'

Speaking after Sunday's triumph, McInnes praised his team's 'big performance' – an especially impressive one given, as will be the case with all Old Firm games this season, no away fans were allowed into the ground.

"Really pleased," he told Sky Sports. "We had to deliver a big performance and we did exactly that. It's not easy coming here, the circumstances you're under and what you face.

2 Naderi scored the winning goal shortly after the half-hour mark at Celtic Park Credit: Getty

"We knew we'd have to overcome a wounded Celtic team. We played with a lot of confidence. I'm disappointed we didn't add to the goal we did score, because we were deserving of that.

"At 1-0, you still think they'll get a chance and we're kicking ourselves a wee bit that we didn't take another chance. It was a worthy win, after what was a disappointing start in the league.

"They came in with a back five, filled the middle of the pitch. In the main, we got it right. In the first 15-20 minutes, our strikers weren't giving us enough but once they started linking the play, everything looked quite calm.

"With someone like [Camilo] Duran up top, we always had to be on our toes. But it was a strong performance."

Next up for Rangers and Celtic

Rangers return to action next month with a home clash against Kilmarnock.

Celtic, meanwhile, hit the road to take on Motherwell.

The next Old Firm showdown is scheduled for January 3 at Ibrox.

Sports.title: Liverpool star ‘who doesn’t belong’ in Premier League has Andoni Iraola raging on touchline
Sports.content:
Liverpool star ‘who doesn’t belong’ in Premier League has Andoni Iraola raging on touchline

Florian Wirtz left Andoni Iraola fuming during Liverpool's clash with Bournemouth on Sunday.

The midfielder was slammed for his first half performance against the Cherries.



3 Wirtz has been told he 'doesn't belong' in the Premier League Credit: Getty

Wirtz ended the opening 45 minutes with the lowest passing accuracy of any Liverpool player.

The Germany international completed just 63 per cent of his attempted passes.

He did end up getting the assist for Alexander Isak's winner as Liverpool beat Bournemouth 1-0.



Deeney on Wirtz

Iraola's frustration with Wirtz on the touchline was spotted by talkSPORT's Troy Deeney.

Speaking on GameDay Live, he said: "Florian Wirtz for me, it's the first time I've seen him live.



"He just doesn't look like he belongs in this league. What I mean by that is, he's clearly talented, clearly he's got the technical ability.

"But it's like he doesn't believe he's going to score and doesn't believe he's going to impact the game. Liverpool need more from him.



"The rest of the team are starting to disbelieve because every time it goes to him, the tempo slows down.

"That means (Bradley) Barcola doesn't get the ball quick, (Cody) Gakpo doesn't get the ball quick, it allows Bournemouth to get back.

"And when they get back, it slows the whole thing down. Iraola just in front of us was absolutely blowing his top."

After Alexander Isak gave the visitors the lead following the interval, Deeney added: "His brain's working quicker than his body.



3 Wirtz had the lowest pass accuracy of any Liverpool player during the first half Credit: Getty

"He's not playing free. In the warm-up, he looks unbelievable. It looks effortless, but when he plays, he's overthinking everything."

Wirtz's Liverpool struggles

Wirtz's woes have continued into the current campaign after a difficult first season at Anfield.

The 23-year-old joined Liverpool form Bayer Leverkusen last summer for a then Premier League record £116.5million.



Despite scoring seven goals and providing nine assists in all competitions, he failed to live up to expectations for the Reds.

Wirtz is yet to register either a goal or an assist in six matches so far this term.

His last goal for the club came in a 3-1 home win over Crystal Palace on April 25.

3 Iraola was visibly frustrated with Wirtz on the touchline Credit: Getty



In contrast, his final season in Germany saw Wirtz score 16 goals and add 15 assists in 45 appearances across all competitions.

Although his current deal runs until 2030, Bayern Munich have recently been credited with an interest.

Sports.title: Pascal Gross makes statement on international future after being left out of Germany squad by Jurgen Klopp
Sports.content:
Pascal Gross makes statement on international future after being left out of Germany squad by Jurgen Klopp

Pascal Gross has confirmed his retirement from international football.

The Brighton midfielder was left out of Jurgen Klopp's first Germany squad but revealed he had already made up his mind about calling time on his international career.



2 Gross earned his final cap for Germany at this summer's World Cup Credit: Getty

Gross had 'already retired'

"Officially – since I don't have social media – I haven't announced my retirement, but I have already retired," the 35-year-old told Sky Sports.

"For me, it was over after the World Cup. I think it's time to wish the new generation nothing but the best and to keep my fingers crossed for them."

Gross, who has been one of the standout players of the Premier League season so far, earned 19 caps for Germany during a three-year international career, scoring once.



He made one appearance at both Euro 2024 and this summer's World Cup.

But he'll now focus on club football, and he's absolutely thriving for Brighton right now – having rejoined the club from Borussia Dortmund two years ago.

Scoring for fun

Gross has scored four goals and provided three assists in all competitions this term, finding the net in Brighton's superb 3-0 Premier League win over Arsenal on Saturday.



Speaking to Match of the Day after that game, Gross said he was 'loving life' right now.

"I thought we showed great intensity, waited for mistakes and punished Arsenal," he reflected. "It was a strong performance, a very complete performance.



"We won the ball high up and attacked really fast. After the last two wins we are full of confidence and wanted to finish really strong before the international break.

"I feel really good. I can't complain. I just try to help the team when I can. I really enjoy life in Brighton – I'm loving it.

2 Gross has scored 37 goals in 252 appearances across two spells with Brighton Credit: Getty

"I know after the international break we play every three days and a lot of the lads are not used to that. It will be tough. I hope we can compete. We have a big squad this season."



Brighton sitting pretty

Brighton will head into the three-week international break no lower than fourth in the Premier League table.

Fabian Hurzeler's Seagulls have won three and drawn one of their opening five games, scoring a league-high 16 goals in the process.

They return to Premier League action next month with a trip to Sunderland, before hosting Lithuania's Kauno Zalgiris in their Conference League opener then entertaining bitter rivals Crystal Palace.

In the meantime, Germany, without Gross, begin their Nations League campaign away to the Netherlands.



Klopp was appointed in July as the successor to Julian Nagelsmann following a disappointing World Cup campaign.

Sports.title: Only a late stroke of luck spared dismal Man United defeat at struggling Fulham, but it's Sir Jim Ratcliffe - not Michael Carrick - who must take the blame for his club's worsening crisis, writes OLIVER HOLT
Sports.content:
There is a pub on Fulham High Street called The Eight Bells.

Paper signs on the windows say that it is reserved for away fans only and on Sunday afternoon, the strains of Manchester United supporters singing in support of their team drifted into the afternoon sunshine before the game.

It is reputed to be Fulham's oldest pub. In fact, there are unsubstantiated claims it is even older than United's back-four. It might have been more appropriate if it was called The Seven Bells, because that is what United got knocked out of them for much of their clash with Alvaro Arbeloa's side at Craven Cottage.

They were outplayed for long periods of the match but escaped with a 1-1 draw after a stroke of luck in the dying minutes brought them a last-gasp equaliser.

They salvaged a little pride but not much. They have five points from their opening five games against Hull City, Ipswich Town, Everton, Manchester City and Fulham.

A season that began with some hopes of them challenging for the title has collapsed into a situation where they are 10 points behind Manchester City before we have even entered the last week of September. Sir Jim Ratcliffe, their minority owner, is an expert on once great things now 'on the slide'. He has added United to his portfolio.

Manchester United are facing more questions than answers after a 1-1 draw away at Fulham

Michael Carrick watched on in dismay as his side looked second best away against Fulham

'It is quite difficult to see how we arrest it,' Sir Jim said of the UK's travails. That sounds like a dispiritingly familiar refrain to United fans.

It is 13 years since they last won the Premier League title and it will be 14 in May. They are too far behind City and Arsenal already to have any chance of ending their drought.

They had some momentum coming into this campaign. Now they have none.

Manager Michael Carrick will get some of the blame for that but this is not his fault. The horror show that is unfolding now is the fault of Sir Jim and his band of hapless executives who masterminded a dreadful summer transfer window that has left United hopelessly adrift of their rivals.

Knocked out of the Carabao Cup by Brighton last week, spurned by the greatest of their young talents, JJ Gabriel, and at war with their own supporters, United had chances and hit the woodwork twice but they looked more predictable and more weary than Fulham.

This was a Fulham, by the way, that were bottom of the table at the start of play but looked more imaginative, more optimistic, more youthful and more coherent than their opponents.

Fulham's point took them above Tottenham Hotspur, who will spend the three weeks of the international break rooted to the foot of the division.

United had spent the first few minutes of the game chasing lengthening shadows. Fulham played the ball about confidently and patiently. They evaded United's half-hearted attempts to press them until a ball was fizzed in to Gonzalo Garcia on the edge of the United box. Garcia snatched at his shot and dragged it wide but it was a chastening start for the visitors.

Lisandro Martinez deflected the ball past a helpless Senne Lammens in the Man United goal

Calvin Bassey wheeled away in celebration after his initial strike eventually led to the first goal

It was a tough watch for Manchester United's travelling fans, who saw a side devoid of energy

When United finally established a foothold in the game, they nearly took the lead. Lisandro Martinez ran on to a loose ball and hit a dipping swerving shot from 25 yards that was destined for the top corner until Bernd Leno launched himself through the air and tipped it wide.

United came close again midway through the half. Matheus Cunha stole the ball away from a Fulham defender as he tried to shepherd it out of play and pulled the ball back for Bruno Fernandes.

Fernandes clipped it towards goal but the ball rolled against the foot of Leno's right-hand post and dribbled away to safety.

United had made the best chances but Fulham had been the better team.

That dynamic shifted after half an hour when Garcia had a golden chance to put Fulham ahead but miskicked in front of goal as he tried to convert Alex Iwobi's cross. Lammens saved well when Sander Berge tried to convert the loose ball.

Then it was the turn of Josh King to go close. King should have been included in Thomas Tuchel's England squad after an outstanding start to this season but was overlooked. Everything about his play in this match showed why he should have been picked.

Fifteen minutes before half-time, he jinked past Luke Shaw with ease and rifled in a shot that Lammens kept out with his right boot.

In the midst of Fulham's missed chances, United hit the woodwork again. Cunha's shot from the edge of the area deflected off a defender and spun up into the air. It was looping over Leno until the goalkeeper got a hand to it and touched it on to the post. United were being outplayed but they were always in the game.

A minute before the break, Marcus Rashford volleyed over from ten yards out. At the other end, King went past Maguire and fell to the ground as Maguire's arm brushed him on his way through.

It was not a foul but nor was it the yellow card that referee Peter Bankes brandished at King.

Matheus Cunha's late deflected strike ensured Manchester United left with something

The second half started slowly but exploded into life just after the hour. Calvin Bassey wrestled the ball away from Cunha on the edge of the United box and unleashed a fierce left-foot drive. Lammens blocked it with his left leg but the ball rebounded to Martinez.

The Argentina defender could not react quickly enough to control it and it bounced off him and back towards goal. Lammens tried to clear it but got his feet in a tangle and deflected it into his own net. Martinez turned away in dismay.

United thought they had equalised minutes later. Bryan Mbeumo curled a shot goalwards and began to wheel away to celebrate before Leno pulled off a magnificent, flying one-handed save that preserved Fulham's lead.

United dominated possession after that but showed little in the way of cutting edge. It took a slice of fortune to drag them level. Fulham held on until two minutes from the end but then Cunha cut in from the left and fired in a shot. Leno had it covered but it deflected off David Affengruber's outstretched foot and bobbled apologetically over the line.

Sports.title: Celtic supporters' bus bursts into FLAMES: Emergency services rush to scene in Glasgow to evacuate fans after Old Firm derby
Sports.content:
A group of football fans suffered a major scare as their coach went up in flames following Sunday's Old Firm derby.

As frustrated Celtic fans headed for home having seen their side lose 1-0 at Parkhead to their bitterest rivals Rangers, the biggest concern of the day was still to come.

As a group of Celtic fans travelled home the rear of their coach caught fire on the A728 near to the Emirates Arena.

Thick black smoke soon dominated the Glasgow sky as fans were quickly evacuated and moved to safety as emergency services rushed to the scene in the east end of the city. Police Scotland have confirmed nobody was injured.

Two fire engines were seen on site with the Clyde Gateway brought to a standstill as the blaze was tackled and eventually halted with stunned fans watching on from the side of the road.

In a statement to the Scottish Sun, McLean's Coaches, who the bus was hired from, said: 'We are aware of the incident involving one of our vehicles on the Clyde Gateway today.

A group of Celtic fans were evacuated as their coach home burst into flames after the match

'The vehicle has been recovered, and we are working with the relevant authorities and parties to establish exactly what happened.

'The cause of the fire has not yet been confirmed, so it would be inappropriate to speculate while enquiries are ongoing.

'Safety is our highest priority, and the vehicle will undergo a full investigation before any further steps are decided.'

It marked the end to a disappointing day for those rooting for Celtic after they were narrowly beaten.

Ryan Naderi's first half strike was enough by the time the final whistle sounded as Celtic's misery was compounded by the fact that they have now lost to Rangers twice in the space of eight days.

Sports.title: Furious Jose Mourinho brings PRINTOUTS of referee 'errors' to tense Madrid derby press conference - and blasts 'poor' officials who 'couldn't handle the pressure' after his side's 2-1 defeat
Sports.content:
A furious Jose Mourinho lashed out at referee Ortiz Arias, claiming he was not qualified to officiate Sunday's Madrid derby.

Mourinho ended up on the losing side as his 10-man Real Madrid lost 2-1 at the Wanda Metropolitano against fierce city rivals Atletico Madrid.

Still seething in the press conference, Mourinho arrived with printed out photos which showed, in his opinion, a series of major calls missed by the referee.

'We could save ourselves the press conference,' an irritated Mourinho began.

'Here they are [shows photos of the possible red cards], two clear reds. It would have been 50 minutes of 11 against nine. All I can do is hug my players, who gave everything, who produced a first half full of class and personality. I prepared the match so we could win it in the second half.'

Rather than pick apart the performance of his players, which saw Dean Huijsen sent off, he focused in on the 'poor' performance of Arias, a referee he does not believe is suitable for the biggest games.

Jose Mourinho was furious at the refereeing performance of Ortiz Arias (right) on Sunday

Mourinho was so livid at the refereeing performance he printed out fouls he felt were missed

'The one who should be happy is the Refereeing Appointments Committee because the whole thing was very strange,' Mourinho's rant continued.

'A week in advance, they already knew who the referee would be, when it used to be 24 hours before. A 41-year-old referee, who has never been an international, that won't be top level.

'The poor guy came here and couldn't handle the pressure.
